# Other International News
* **Trump administration issues more ICC sanctions:** The Trump administration [sanctioned](https://substack.com/redirect/a81cf030-7d65-4339-9a75-702a5779a202?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye on Tuesday as the court pursues investigations into Israel's crimes in Gaza and the West Bank.
* Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu celebrated the move on X, called the ICC a "kangaroo court" and praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio for making its officials "face consequences." Rubio says his campaign aims to "dismantle" the court.
* Washington has sanctioned at least 11 ICC officials, including prosecutor Karim Khan, who secured arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant on charges of committing war crimes in Gaza.
* **Bolivia arrests major Trump-linked right-wing operative over shooting of activist:** Bolivian police have [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/69e4e0a5-0b05-4875-b231-ea36d6ff4d83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Fernando Cerimedo, an Argentine political operative with connections to President Donald Trump's former campaign manager, as the main suspect in the shooting of his former partner, lawyer and activist Nadia Beller.
* Beller, 33, was shot three times outside a hotel in Santa Cruz de la Sierra on Monday night by two attackers disguised as delivery workers, according to La Nacion. She survived and is hospitalized in stable condition.
* Cerimedo was detained early Tuesday at Viru Viru airport trying to board a flight to Buenos Aires. He denies involvement, calling it a "campaign against him."
* Cerimedo is a business partner of Brad Parscale, Donald Trump's former campaign manager, in the Buenos Aires consultancy Numen. The firm worked the campaigns of Javier Milei in Argentina, Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia, and Nasry Asfura in Honduras, all right-wing victories.
* **Half of Venezuela 's oil is being exported to the U.S.:** About half of Venezuela's oil production is now being [exported](https://substack.com/redirect/a53e0323-34ae-4b08-bdb0-58d6e46cf189?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the United States, Kyle Haustveit, an undersecretary in the U.S. Department of Energy, said Tuesday.
* "In the last couple of months, we're seeing north of 500,000 barrels, or approximately half of the production coming out of Venezuela, coming to the United States...to the refineries that were built specifically for that crude," Haustveit told an industry event in Houston.
* The surge marks a sharp redirection of Venezuela's oil away from China, its longtime top buyer, toward the U.S. At the end of 2025, only about 135,000 of Venezuela's roughly 1 million barrels per day went to American refineries.
* **Pakistan will challenge Imran Khan ruling:** Pakistan's government said on Wednesday it would [challenge](https://substack.com/redirect/873965c8-6a59-4c2e-9039-bd8a19beed14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Supreme Court order requiring jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be transferred within two days to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad and given access to his personal physician.
* Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ruling was "not within four walls of the law," arguing that convicted prisoners must be treated in jail or at a public hospital. The government will seek a review and modification of the order, according to AFP.
* Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023. His lawyers say he has lost significant vision in his right eye. His PTI party welcomed the order and demanded it be implemented immediately.
* **Israel says strike on Syria intended to block Turkish military buildup:** Israel [said](https://substack.com/redirect/5989e989-facf-47b2-a5e3-0e9e240e5c1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its eight strikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib province were intended to prevent a Turkish military deployment, according to Axios and the Israeli prime minister's office.
* The attacks damaged the runway and storage facilities, with no casualties reported, according to regional media.
* Israel's Prime Minister's Office claimed Syria was about to breach a "status quo" security agreement by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at the base.
* A Turkish official denied any Turkish presence there, telling Axios: "Israel is inventing pretexts to bomb neighboring countries and destabilize the region."

* **Zelenskyy fires senior aide amid corruption probe:** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [dismissed](https://substack.com/redirect/4b5e238c-03aa-42a8-bbe1-17778ed14080?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) deputy presidential office head Iryna Mudra after anti-corruption investigators searched her office in a money-laundering probe.
* The latest scandal follows a series of corruption investigations that have reached officials close to Zelenskyy, including the resignation of his former Chief of Staff Andriy Yermak last year.
* The political crisis widened after recently ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for a mechanism to hold national elections despite martial law, arguing that Ukraine's political system had become focused on preserving itself and resisting change.
* **Liberia agrees to accept up to 1,200 U.S. deportees:** Liberia said it will [receive](https://substack.com/redirect/4113fd6c-4fb2-4b1e-9721-e039a3a5e614?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as many as 1,200 people deported from the United States who are not Liberian nationals, in one of the largest such arrangements under the Trump administration's expanded use of third-country removals.
* The transfers are expected to take place over the next year, with an initial group of 20 due to arrive Thursday. Liberian officials said the group will include people from Africa, North and South America, and the Caribbean.
* The deal is part of a broader U.S. policy of deporting migrants to countries other than their own, including people who may have U.S. protection orders barring return to their home countries.
* **Iraqi resistance leader decries U.S. control over Iraq 's oil money and airspace: **Abu Ala al-Walai, secretary-general of the Iraqi armed group Kataib Sayyed al-Shuhada, [denounced](https://substack.com/redirect/78177db6-f969-4c4b-8f01-06ed02f43977?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. economic and military domination of Iraq in a statement on X on Tuesday.
* "In my country, oil is sold, but Iraq has no right to dispose of its own money because there is an American occupation," he wrote. He said Iraqi planes "don't fly in our skies except with America's permission," and that Washington blocks Iraq from buying electricity from Turkey or Iran, striking deals with China, or contracting firms like Siemens to fix its power grid. "The people want full sovereignty for Iraq. So where is the sovereignty, gentlemen?" he wrote.
* **South Korea says Trump military drill cuts may be pressure on Seoul over Iran war, investment:** South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun [said](https://substack.com/redirect/38f6a393-dc05-495f-bff4-301278eb6d75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday that U.S. President Donald Trump's order to sharply reduce joint U.S.-South Korean military exercises appeared partly intended to pressure Seoul over Washington's efforts in the Iran war and other unresolved issues, including South Korea's pledged $350 billion investment in the United States, Reuters reported.
* Cho said Trump's move appeared aimed at "breaking a stalemate in the Iran war," while also sending a message to North Korea. Seoul and Washington announced Wednesday that their annual joint drills would be shortened from 11 days to five and some field training scaled back.

Palestinian child dies of malnutrition in Gaza. Nearly 470 attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank in a week. Land seizures, settler attacks and detentions reported across the occupied West Bank. UN: Gaza remains world's deadliest place for aid workers in 2025 for third consecutive year. Israel announces probe into two high-profile Gaza massacres. United Arab Emirates halts all trade with Iran after accusing it of launching missiles. President Donald Trump calls Hormuz "New U.S. Territory." Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf visits Iraq, lauds "resistance." Pentagon considering Gulf drawdown. Vessel struck, "completely" disabled off of Mokha. Missile strikes in Yemen kill three, including a child, in Hodeidah. Israeli forces continue military activity, demolitions in southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire." Lebanese army chief: Israel keeps attacking even as army implements agreement. Hezbollah MP: Resistance will confront any Israeli move on Ali Al-Taher. Primary results from Florida, Alaska, Wyoming, and California. Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon criticizes party leadership. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Israel escalates its attacks on Gaza, killing 17, wounding 38 over the past 24 hours: An Israeli strike on a seaside cafe on Tuesday killed seven Palestinians and wounded 14, with Al Jazeera confirming at least one child was among those killed. "We don't know what we're supposed to deal with anymore. Do we deal with the Israelis? Or the sun burning us inside the tents? Or the water--waking up at 6 a.m. to go get water? Or do we deal with the winter that is still coming, when we'll also suffer from the weather?" Eyewitness Abu Ahmed said. Drop Site 's Mohamed Ahmed submitted video reports from the scene of the port attack, available and . At least nine Palestinians were killed and 15 wounded on Wednesday in an Israeli airstrike on the Municipalities Police headquarters in Gaza City, according to Gaza's Interior Ministry. The strike hit during a busy time in the middle of day and close to a crowded municipal park. from Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed of the police building attack shows ambulances arriving as people rush to carry the dead and wounded, including a woman and a child. "Every day we say, 'Tomorrow there's hope. There is still hope,' while the number of martyrs keeps rising. Let people feel for us. Yesterday, it was the port. Today, the municipal park, full of children. Every day, they take revenge on us," eyewitness Abu Al-Baha said. Separately, an earlier Israeli strike on a motorcycle in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza killed one Palestinian. Gaza's Interior Ministry said Israeli attacks on the civil police force are meant to cripple the police and "spread chaos within Palestinian society. Hamas rejected the Israeli military's claim that resistance leaders were targeted as "baseless." The group said the attack, coming after recent meetings with mediators and "Board of Peace" member Jared Kushner aimed at advancing the ceasefire agreement, showed Netanyahu's government was deliberately seeking to undermine those efforts. Hamas called on mediators, particularly the Trump administration, to take immediate action to halt the escalation and pressure Israel to abide by the agreement. Palestinian child dies of malnutrition in Gaza: A Palestinian girl from severe malnutrition on Tuesday as Israel continues to restrict food and other necessities entering Gaza. Since the ceasefire began, Israel has allowed in only 35.3% of the minimum agreed aid deliveries, averaging 211.8 trucks daily against the required 600, a document shared by Palestinian authorities with mediators on Sunday showed. The IPC warns that 74,200 children in the Strip require treatment for acute malnutrition through April 2027, including more than 11,400 severe cases. Without sustained aid, nearly 1.9 million Palestinians could face acute food insecurity by December. Nearly 470 attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank in a week: Israeli forces and settlers conducted at least 467 attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank in one week, to the Palestinian prime minister's office. At least 75 Palestinian homes and structures were also demolished, the office said, calling the attacks "relentless escalation of violence, dispossession, and destruction." Israel places Palestinian journalist Mohamed Awad under administrative detention: Palestinian journalist and Drop Site contributor Mohamed Awad has been placed under administrative detention by Israeli authorities, according to journalist Mutassem Saqf Al-Hait. Awad was arrested from his home in the village of Beitunia, near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, on August 12 by the Israeli military. Administrative detention is a legal mechanism that allows Israeli authorities to imprison Palestinians indefinitely without charge or trial. Land seizures, settler attacks and detentions reported across the occupied West Bank: Israeli forces at least 30 Palestinians in raids across the occupied West Bank between Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Society, while Israeli authorities and settlers carried out land seizures, outpost expansion and the continued siege of Palestinian homes. The detainees included journalist Abdulrahman Hassan from Bethlehem, while Israeli forces separately arrested Palestinian Jerusalem Affairs Minister after raiding his home in Silwan. Ramallah: Israeli forces and critically wounded a Palestinian man during a Tuesday evening raid on Al-Amari refugee camp in Al-Bireh, in the central West Bank, according to the Palestinian Information Center. Israeli authorities approximately 1,152 dunams (285 acres) of land in Sinjil, Al-Lubban al-Sharqiya and Qaryut as "state property" to expand the Karmei Oz settlement, the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said. Nablus : For a second straight day, Israeli settlers blocked roads in Beit Imrin, northwest of Nablus, isolating families and cutting farmers off from their land, amid a push to build a new settlement outpost nearby. Settlers, backed by Israeli forces, also continued to besiege three Palestinian homes in the Ras Al-Ain area of Qusra for the 11th consecutive day. Jenin : Palestinian Ahmed Al-Hatnawi Radio Al-Shams that Israeli forces etched the number "44" on his forehead and arm after detaining him during a raid in Qabatiyah, Haaretz reported. "As if we were animals and beasts," he said, describing the practice as deliberate humiliation. Al-Hatnawi said Israeli forces took him to a makeshift interrogation site, questioned him for roughly two hours, and threatened him. UN: Gaza remains world 's deadliest place for aid workers in 2025 for third consecutive year: Gaza the world's deadliest place for aid workers in 2025 for the third consecutive year, with 186 killed in Israeli attacks despite the ceasefire declared in October, according to the UN humanitarian office (OCHA) in a statement to mark World Humanitarian Day. 68% percent of those killed in Gaza died in aerial bombardments. Globally, 350 humanitarian workers were killed in 2025, the second-highest annual toll on record, while 907 aid workers were victims of violence. Sudan recorded a record 71 aid worker deaths. Israel announces probe into two high profile Gaza massacres: The Israeli military on Wednesday that it would launch criminal investigations into two high profile attacks in Gaza, including the killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab and six members of her family in January 2024, and the massacre of 15 Palestinian aid workers in southern Gaza in March 2025. The military said it would not launch criminal investigations into three other attacks that killed aid workers from World Central Kitchen and Doctors Without Borders. The decisions followed reviews by the Israeli military's fact-finding mechanism, which is officially tasked with examining exceptional operational incidents during wartime. In its statement, the Israeli military acknowledged for the first time that it opened fire on the vehicle carrying Hind Rajab and her family after previously denying involvement in the incident and falsely claiming that its forces were not present in the area. an in-depth investigation into the killing of Hind Rajab by Al Jazeera 's Fault Lines in "The Night Won't End." An investigation by Forensic Architecture into the aid worker massacre found that Israeli soldiers fired nearly a thousand bullets during the attack and that a number of aid workers were executed by Israeli soldiers at point blank range. Read Drop Site 's coverage . Iran UAE halts all trade with Iran after accusing it of launching missiles: Iranian air defenses detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, the first falling outside its territorial waters and the second within them, the UAE Defense Ministry on Tuesday, with a phone alert warning residents of a "potential missile threat." The UAE Foreign Ministry then announced it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran until further notice, citing regional escalation. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei "completely rejected" the claim that it launched missiles targeting Emirati territory, calling it damaging to efforts to build regional trust. Trump calls Hormuz "New U.S. Territory": U.S. President Donald Trump a map labeling the Strait of Hormuz "NEW U.S. Territory," and, in a separate post, said no talks with Iran are underway and that the U.S. naval blockade remains "in full force and effect." Trump also claimed Hormuz is "open and operating" and that all naval mines have been removed or detonated. Just three transits were recorded on August 16 and 10 crossings on August 17. Kpler said vessels continue using Iran's unilateral routing scheme, with none recorded through the conventional Hormuz traffic-separation system or southern Omani routes yesterday. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf Tuesday that "until the United States implements its commitments under the memorandum, including lifting the blockade, releasing frozen assets, lifting oil sanctions, ending threats and military operations on all fronts, and the other agreed conditions, the strait will not reopen." Ghalibaf visits Iraq, lauds "resistance": Ghalibaf arrived in Iraq on Wednesday for a three-day visit. Speaking at the site where former General Qassem Soleimani was killed, Ghalibaf said, "Today's visit to Iraq is aimed at strengthening the new order in the region and accelerating mutual cooperation among all countries of the region, without the intervention of foreign powers." Referring to Iran-backed militias in Iraq, Ghalibaf added, "After years of experience in Iraq, the resistance has gone beyond the borders of the two countries and has become an influential force at the regional and global levels Pentagon considering Gulf drawdown: The Pentagon is assessing whether to its Persian Gulf military presence after Iranian strikes exposed the vulnerability of Washington's regional base network, eight officials told The Washington Post on Tuesday. CENTCOM normally stations about 40,000 troops across nearly 20 sites. More than 200 U.S. facilities have been damaged or destroyed since U.S. and Israel launched war; strikes killed six troops in Kuwait and four in Jordan, while U.S. defenses burned through more than 1,000 Patriot and THAAD interceptors. Officials have considered shifting forces west toward Jordan, Israel, or Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast. Rubio talks with UAE national security official: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio by phone Tuesday with UAE National Security Adviser Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, discussing "regional security issues" including recent developments in Lebanon and the Strait of Hormuz, the State Department said in a statement. Rubio continued to call for "freedom of navigation" through the Strait, and urged further U.S.-UAE coordination against Iran and its allies. Yemen Vessel struck, "completely" disabled off of Mokha: A cargo ship was by multiple unidentified projectiles about 40 nautical miles southeast of Mokha, Yemen, resulting in a "complete constructive loss" of the vessel, United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Wednesday. The ship was unmanned at the time of the incident, local authorities said. Missile strikes kill three, including a child, in Hodeidah: Three civilians, including a child, were after two Ansarallah ballistic missiles reportedly struck Al-Khawkhah district in Yemen's southern Hodeidah province, the Saudi-backed and government-aligned National Resistance Forces said on Wednesday. Lebanon Israeli forces continue military activity, demolitions in southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire": Israeli warplanes strikes on multiple locations in southern Lebanon early Wednesday, according to Lebanese media. The strikes, according to the Lebanese outlet Al Mayadeen, targeted the important Ali Al-Tahir heights and the area of Kfar Rumman. In Nabatieh, two young men were and others wounded when a suspicious object believed to be unexploded ordnance left from previous Israeli attacks detonated near the earthen berm between Mayfadoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqieh, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. Israeli forces demolition operations Tuesday evening in Talousseh, Zawtar Sharqieh and Kounin, destroying several homes as attacks continued across southern Lebanon, L'Orient Today reported. Forces demolished a water reservoir supplying Mansouri, destroyed two three-story buildings in the village and demolished at least one building. Lebanese army chief: Israel keeps attacking even as army implements agreement: The Lebanese military continues carrying out its obligations under the U.S.-brokered framework agreement while Israeli forces continue their "attacks and violations," Lebanese Army commander Rodolphe Haykal via NNA. Haykal made the remarks during a meeting with Edward Gabriel, president of the American Task Force for Lebanon. Hezbollah MP: Resistance will confront any Israeli move on Ali Al-Taher: Hezbollah Member of Parliament Hassan Ezzeddine the group would not abandon the Ali Al-Taher heights and would "confront any act of aggression" against the strategic position with all available capabilities, speaking to the Russian news outlet Sputnik. Israeli forces have been dropping explosives around the heights almost daily, amid reports Israel could be preparing a larger operation there. "Ali Al-Taher is one of the resistance's key positions," Ezzeddine said, adding that Iranian assistance would provide additional strength. "If assistance comes from Iran, that would be light upon light," he said. He suggested Iran, which has established deterrence against Israeli strikes on Beirut, may act if Israel acts against the strategic heights. U.S. News Tuesday 's primary results: State Rep.Angie Nixon defeated former Lt. Col. Alex Vindman in the Florida Democratic Senate Primary. Vindman** had a significant fundraising advantage over Nixon, having raised $16.3 million to Nixon's $975,000 before the primary, but Nixon handily defeated him, receiving 56% of the vote in Tuesday night's primary. DSA-member Nixon will face GOP Sen. Ashley Moody in the November general election. In an interview with CNN following her victory, Nixon Democratic leaders Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer should face scrutiny as too many "corporate-established Democrats" are beholden to companies rather than ordinary people. Rep. Jared Moskowitz defeated his DSA-backed opponent Oliver Larkin in the Democratic primary for Florida's 23rd congressional district. Moskowitz, one of the Democratic Party's more ardent supporters of Israel, used the occasion of his primary victory to taunt political streamer Hasan Piker , offering his "condolences" to Piker after the AP called the race. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz won her primary in the redrawn 20th congressional district, defeating four Black opponents in the majority Black district. Rep. Byron Donalds easily won the Republican nomination in the Florida gubernatorial primary on Tuesday, and will face Democrat David Jolly in the November election to replace term-limited Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis. Republican Rep. Cory Mills , under investigation for sexual misconduct by the House Ethics Committee, lost to Ryan Elijah , a former local TV anchor, in Florida's 7th district. President Trump had endorsed Mills, making him the second Republican (after Tennessee Rep. Andy Ogles) to lose a primary with the president's endorsement. Elijah will face Democrat Bale Dalton , a former NASA official, in the November general election. Democratic Rep.Mary Peltola a tentative, 2-point lead over GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's nonpartisan primary. Both are projected to advance to the November general election, in a race that could determine the control of the Senate. Progressive state Sen. Aisha Wahab a narrow lead over the moderate and AIPAC-backed public transit official Melissa Hernandez in the special primary to replace California Rep. Eric Swalwell. As of Wednesday morning, Wahab leads Hernandez by 2 percentage points, according to NBC News. Eric Barlow , a rancher and state senator, the Trump-endorsed public education superintendent Megan Degenfelder in Wyoming's gubernatorial primary on Tuesday. His victory makes him nearly certain to win the general election in the deep-red state, where voters gave Trump his highest margin of victory in the 2024 presidential election. Trump administration moves to repeal Clinton-era "roadless rule": The U.S. Forest Service a proposal Tuesday to repeal the 2001 "roadless rule," opening nearly 45 million acres of national forest wilderness to road construction and logging and eliminating protections that have stood for a quarter century, including for nine million undeveloped acres in Alaska's Tongass National Forest. Environmentalists have warned that the move endangers drinking water supplies and wildlife habitats, and ecologists told the New York Times that new roads could increase wildfire risk by bringing more human activity into previously undisturbed areas. The proposal, expected to be published in the Federal Register this week before a public comment period, follows Trump's push for a 25% increase in national forest logging and Rollins' prior declaration of an "emergency situation," which allowed the Forest Service to fast-track timber production by curtailing environmental review. Trump pauses new 50% Canada tariffs for three days, cites pending trade deal : President Donald Trump Tuesday night he was pausing the 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days, saying on Truth Social that the U.S. and Canada "have a DEAL!" pending finalization, following talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The tariffs, which had been set to take effect early Wednesday under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, targeted goods including alcohol, hockey equipment, cement, and dairy products. Whistleblower alleges Trump antisemitism task force pressured universities despite lacking evidence: A whistleblower complaint from former DOJ civil rights attorney Haley Van Erem , made public by Rep. Jamie Raskin on Tuesday, the Trump administration's antisemitism task force pursued "predetermined" outcomes against Harvard, Brown, and Columbia despite little evidence supporting systemic Title VI violations, overruling career attorneys who objected to the investigations. U.S. quietly deporting Mexican migrants to Guatemala, Honduras instead of Mexico : The Trump administration has been deportees from Mexico to Guatemala and Honduras rather than back to Mexico, despite Mexico's willingness to accept all its citizens, according to two Department of Homeland Security officials who spoke to CBS News on Tuesday. Minnesota AG sues Texas Gov. Abbott over refusal to extradite ICE agent : Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison Texas Gov. Greg Abbott on Tuesday to compel the extradition of ICE agent Christian Castro , who faces Minnesota charges of assault and falsely reporting a crime in connection with the January shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis. Ellison warned Castro could be released from Texas custody as soon as August 26 under a 90-day detention limit and potentially flee to Mexico, where the lawsuit says he has discussed marrying a woman and buying a house. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Trump administration issues more ICC sanctions: The Trump administration International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye on Tuesday as the court pursues investigations into Israel's crimes in Gaza and the West Bank. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu celebrated the move on X, called the ICC a "kangaroo court" and praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio for making its officials "face consequences." Rubio says his campaign aims to "dismantle" the court. Washington has sanctioned at least 11 ICC officials, including prosecutor Karim Khan, who secured arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant on charges of committing war crimes in Gaza. Bolivia arrests major Trump-linked right-wing operative over shooting of activist: Bolivian police have Fernando Cerimedo, an Argentine political operative with connections to President Donald Trump's former campaign manager, as the main suspect in the shooting of his former partner, lawyer and activist Nadia Beller. Beller, 33, was shot three times outside a hotel in Santa Cruz de la Sierra on Monday night by two attackers disguised as delivery workers, according to La Nacion. She survived and is hospitalized in stable condition. Cerimedo was detained early Tuesday at Viru Viru airport trying to board a flight to Buenos Aires. He denies involvement, calling it a "campaign against him." Cerimedo is a business partner of Brad Parscale, Donald Trump's former campaign manager, in the Buenos Aires consultancy Numen. The firm worked the campaigns of Javier Milei in Argentina, Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia, and Nasry Asfura in Honduras, all right-wing victories. Half of Venezuela 's oil is being exported to the U.S.: About half of Venezuela's oil production is now being to the United States, Kyle Haustveit, an undersecretary in the U.S. Department of Energy, said Tuesday. "In the last couple of months, we're seeing north of 500,000 barrels, or approximately half of the production coming out of Venezuela, coming to the United States...to the refineries that were built specifically for that crude," Haustveit told an industry event in Houston. The surge marks a sharp redirection of Venezuela's oil away from China, its longtime top buyer, toward the U.S. At the end of 2025, only about 135,000 of Venezuela's roughly 1 million barrels per day went to American refineries. Pakistan will challenge Imran Khan ruling: Pakistan's government said on Wednesday it would a Supreme Court order requiring jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be transferred within two days to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad and given access to his personal physician. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ruling was "not within four walls of the law," arguing that convicted prisoners must be treated in jail or at a public hospital. The government will seek a review and modification of the order, according to AFP. Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023. His lawyers say he has lost significant vision in his right eye. His PTI party welcomed the order and demanded it be implemented immediately. Israel says strike on Syria intended to block Turkish military buildup: Israel its eight strikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib province were intended to prevent a Turkish military deployment, according to Axios and the Israeli prime minister's office. The attacks damaged the runway and storage facilities, with no casualties reported, according to regional media. Israel's Prime Minister's Office claimed Syria was about to breach a "status quo" security agreement by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at the base. A Turkish official denied any Turkish presence there, telling Axios: "Israel is inventing pretexts to bomb neighboring countries and destabilize the region." Zelenskyy fires senior aide amid corruption probe: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy deputy presidential office head Iryna Mudra after anti-corruption investigators searched her office in a money-laundering probe. The latest scandal follows a series of corruption investigations that have reached officials close to Zelenskyy, including the resignation of his former Chief of Staff Andriy Yermak last year. The political crisis widened after recently ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for a mechanism to hold national elections despite martial law, arguing that Ukraine's political system had become focused on preserving itself and resisting change. Liberia agrees to accept up to 1,200 U.S. deportees: Liberia said it will as many as 1,200 people deported from the United States who are not Liberian nationals, in one of the largest such arrangements under the Trump administration's expanded use of third-country removals. The transfers are expected to take place over the next year, with an initial group of 20 due to arrive Thursday. Liberian officials said the group will include people from Africa, North and South America, and the Caribbean. The deal is part of a broader U.S. policy of deporting migrants to countries other than their own, including people who may have U.S. protection orders barring return to their home countries. Iraqi resistance leader decries U.S. control over Iraq 's oil money and airspace: Abu Ala al-Walai, secretary-general of the Iraqi armed group Kataib Sayyed al-Shuhada, U.S. economic and military domination of Iraq in a statement on X on Tuesday. "In my country, oil is sold, but Iraq has no right to dispose of its own money because there is an American occupation," he wrote. He said Iraqi planes "don't fly in our skies except with America's permission," and that Washington blocks Iraq from buying electricity from Turkey or Iran, striking deals with China, or contracting firms like Siemens to fix its power grid. "The people want full sovereignty for Iraq. So where is the sovereignty, gentlemen?" he wrote. South Korea says Trump military drill cuts may be pressure on Seoul over Iran war, investment: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun Wednesday that U.S. President Donald Trump's order to sharply reduce joint U.S.-South Korean military exercises appeared partly intended to pressure Seoul over Washington's efforts in the Iran war and other unresolved issues, including South Korea's pledged $350 billion investment in the United States, Reuters reported. Cho said Trump's move appeared aimed at "breaking a stalemate in the Iran war," while also sending a message to North Korea. | | Dear Peter, This weekend, Rep. Emily Randall and I showed up to the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma, Washington for an unannounced visit. We went there to see for ourselves what was happening inside the facility. We found that we had been misled about the hunger strike, including how many detainees were participating and who was taking part. Folks, reportedly 140 people refused meals for nearly a week. This is the 20th time this year that detainees have used a hunger strike to demand humane treatment. Since our visit, detainees in two units have ended their hunger strike after the GEO Group reportedly promised new menus, larger portions and better food. They are giving the facility until Thursday to make good on those promises, and have said they will resume their strike if conditions do not improve. We spoke with one person who participated. He told us they were protesting the lack of appropriate medical care, as well as food that is nutritious and served on time. He is paraplegic and lives with a chronic condition. He told us he is being denied the medical care he needs. **_These are human beings crying out for help. They deserve to be heard._** As a mother, as a physician, and as a member of Congress, I know everyone deserves humane conditions and access to basic medical care. My job is to conduct oversight and ensure the government is telling us the truth. What I saw this weekend raises serious questions about whether that is happening. The facility is short-staffed, including at least four openings in the kitchen, even as the number of detainees continues to increase. Our tax dollars should never be used to pay for-profit institutions to deny people basic necessities. **And promises are not enough. We need to make sure conditions actually improve.** That is why I need you to help us demand answers and accountability. [**Will you join me in raising your voice and signing our petition calling for humane conditions at the Northwest Detention Center today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137523143/641074728/-999302982?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMDk5MDQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTUwMDI5NTgtZTY5Yi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=B685uZSQBEVAA4UTRhRUSdDp40E1qjRaX2gX5o1ASv0=&emci=a637002b-399b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=55002958-e69b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=9506338)

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Peter, This weekend, Rep. Emily Randall and I showed up to the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma, Washington for an unannounced visit. We went there to see for ourselves what was happening inside the facility. We found that we had been misled about the hunger strike, including how many detainees were participating and who was taking part. Folks, reportedly 140 people refused meals for nearly a week. This is the 20th time this year that detainees have used a hunger strike to demand humane treatment. Since our visit, detainees in two units have ended their hunger strike after the GEO Group reportedly promised new menus, larger portions and better food. They are giving the facility until Thursday to make good on those promises, and have said they will resume their strike if conditions do not improve. We spoke with one person who participated. He told us they were protesting the lack of appropriate medical care, as well as food that is nutritious and served on time. He is paraplegic and lives with a chronic condition. He told us he is being denied the medical care he needs. These are human beings crying out for help. They deserve to be heard. As a mother, as a physician, and as a member of Congress, I know everyone deserves humane conditions and access to basic medical care. My job is to conduct oversight and ensure the government is telling us the truth. What I saw this weekend raises serious questions about whether that is happening. The facility is short-staffed, including at least four openings in the kitchen, even as the number of detainees continues to increase. Our tax dollars should never be used to pay for-profit institutions to deny people basic necessities. And promises are not enough. We need to make sure conditions actually improve. That is why I need you to help us demand answers and accountability. | | Your scrutiny and concern matter. Together, we can make sure the people inside that facility are not forgotten and that those responsible are held accountable. Stay loud, Dr. Maxine Dexter | | | | | Maxine Dexter is a critical care physician with decades of experience using facts and following science to help her patients. * * *
Given everything happening this week, I keep thinking about how easily the MAGA movement can manufacture a lie and watch it take over the national conversation. It's maddening.
I'm not going to linger again on Donald Trump's DOJ targeting my company on the "strength" of Laura Loomer's conspiracy theory reporting, but there's a pattern here worth diagnosing -- because once you see it, you understand how insane our discourse has become.
Politicians have always lied. There have always been grifters and shameless people who see our politics as a way to grab money or power. I'm not naive about that.
What's different now is that there's no accountability. When someone is caught lying or cheating or stealing, nothing pulls it back to earth -- no consequence proportional to the lie, no price for the cruelty, no cost for being deliberately full of shit.
There is no gravity left in American politics.
Start with what happened to Dean Withers this week, a fellow YouTuber I've never met. From what he's laid out on Instagram, a MAGA operative built a fake profile using photos of a real thirteen-year-old girl and invented a sexual assault out of thin air to burn his reputation down.
I want to be careful -- these are serious allegations, and I always lean toward believing victims. But the evidence he's presented that this "victim" never existed looks credible.
What do you have to believe about the world to steal a child's face and accuse someone of raping her? That you'll get away with it.
And you might -- because there's no gravity.
Take the NYT story this weekend that Trump's DOJ opened an investigation into my business. We'll fight it, and it'll be fine -- but understand the pattern, because you'll see it everywhere: the lie doesn't have to become true anymore. It just has to _activate_ something.
A fake allegation activates an algorithm. A bogus report activates the police. A smear activates the media. Loomer's "reporting" apparently gets the Department of Justice poking around my business -- and suddenly the person being lied about is the one spending their money, reputation, and sanity proving that something that never happened never happened.
The liar gets five minutes. The victim gets lawyers, legal fees, and anguish. We've transferred the cost of the lie from the liar to the person they lied about.
Six weeks ago I wrote about Pete Buttigieg, after someone falsely reported him to CPS for abusing his four-year-old twins. The allegation was bullshit, but the process it triggered was very real -- as it should be when allegations are that serious. Police showed up. His kids were sent to their grandparents.
I called that piece "This is how they pick us off," because this cruelty doesn't just hurt the target -- it scares good people out of public life. Somebody watches what happened to Pete and decides that running for school board isn't worth putting their family through it.
Here's the half I missed the first time. It's not quite right that there are no consequences. There are. We've just gotten very good at making the victims pay them.
Pete paid. Dean is paying, in death threats. I'm paying. What are the people manufacturing this shit paying? Where's the accountability for the person who reported Pete to CPS? Where's the accountability for Loomer?

Go back to 2024. Vance and Trump invented a lie about immigrants in Ohio eating people's pets, and millions swallowed it whole because it flattered the ugliest corner of the internet. Vance went on national television that weekend and admitted out loud that he'll invent stories to jerk the media around.
What happened to him? Nothing. The media thanked him and booked him for the next hit. The lasting legacy of that lie isn't that JD Vance is a grotesque liar -- it's a catchy TikTok song stuck in my head.
That's what covering politics like sports does: Jon Ossoff gets dinged for name-dropping Trump's alleged mistress in a speech -- too far, below the belt -- while the other side fabricates a child's sexual assault to annihilate one of our most effective activists.
These things are not equivalent, and pretending they are is how we got here.
I'm done fighting with one hand tied behind my back, and you should be too. And before someone deliberately misunderstands me: I'm not saying we become them. I'm saying we stop pretending we're playing the same game.
That's what I mean by the next version of the Democratic Party -- one willing to throw a punch, for the people it loves and the Americans the MAGA machine poisons every day.
You don't beat a lie by lying harder. You beat it by refusing to reward it -- by calling bullshit bullshit, by imposing consequences, by restoring some gravity.
Because a system without consequences doesn't just tolerate liars -- it selects for them. If lying costs nothing, you get more liars. If cruelty makes you famous, you get more cruelty. If shamelessness buys followers and TV contracts, you get more shameless people chasing power. And if decency means your kids get threatened and your life gets turned upside down because someone with an internet connection made something up, decent people decide it isn't worth it.
That's how you get the Tate brothers, George Santos, Donald Trump. What kind of person thrives where shame is a disadvantage and shamelessness is a strategy?
So how do we fix it? There's no one neat policy -- government, courts, media, platforms, parties, and you all have a role. But the principle is the same: consequences again.
If Dean can find whoever did this, he should sue them for everything they own, and the platforms that spread it should pay too. When you destroy a life with a lie, that lie should cost you something. I hope Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings and Fox News for the lies they've told about him. I've been thinking hard about my own options against Laura Loomer, and it's a hard road -- which tells you exactly where the burden sits.
Six weeks ago I told you this is how they pick us off. This is the other half: this is how the worst people replace them. It's how you get Trump.
A system without gravity created the conditions for him, and getting rid of him won't be enough, because the incentives that produced him will still be there, waiting for the next guy.
Nothing changes until there are consequences again.
Nothing changes until gravity comes back.

Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. Given everything happening this week, I keep thinking about how easily the MAGA movement can manufacture a lie and watch it take over the national conversation. It's maddening. I'm not going to linger again on Donald Trump's DOJ targeting my company on the "strength" of Laura Loomer's conspiracy theory reporting, but there's a pattern here worth diagnosing -- because once you see it, you understand how insane our discourse has become. Politicians have always lied. There have always been grifters and shameless people who see our politics as a way to grab money or power. I'm not naive about that. What's different now is that there's no accountability. When someone is caught lying or cheating or stealing, nothing pulls it back to earth -- no consequence proportional to the lie, no price for the cruelty, no cost for being deliberately full of shit. There is no gravity left in American politics. Start with what happened to Dean Withers this week, a fellow YouTuber I've never met. From what he's laid out on Instagram, a MAGA operative built a fake profile using photos of a real thirteen-year-old girl and invented a sexual assault out of thin air to burn his reputation down. I want to be careful -- these are serious allegations, and I always lean toward believing victims. But the evidence he's presented that this "victim" never existed looks credible. What do you have to believe about the world to steal a child's face and accuse someone of raping her? That you'll get away with it. And you might -- because there's no gravity. Take the NYT story this weekend that Trump's DOJ opened an investigation into my business. We'll fight it, and it'll be fine -- but understand the pattern, because you'll see it everywhere: the lie doesn't have to become true anymore. It just has to activate something. A fake allegation activates an algorithm. A bogus report activates the police. A smear activates the media. Loomer's "reporting" apparently gets the Department of Justice poking around my business -- and suddenly the person being lied about is the one spending their money, reputation, and sanity proving that something that never happened never happened. The liar gets five minutes. The victim gets lawyers, legal fees, and anguish. We've transferred the cost of the lie from the liar to the person they lied about. Six weeks ago I wrote about Pete Buttigieg, after someone falsely reported him to CPS for abusing his four-year-old twins. The allegation was bullshit, but the process it triggered was very real -- as it should be when allegations are that serious. Police showed up. His kids were sent to their grandparents. I called that piece "This is how they pick us off," because this cruelty doesn't just hurt the target -- it scares good people out of public life. Somebody watches what happened to Pete and decides that running for school board isn't worth putting their family through it. Here's the half I missed the first time. It's not quite right that there are no consequences. There are. We've just gotten very good at making the victims pay them. Pete paid. Dean is paying, in death threats. I'm paying. What are the people manufacturing this shit paying? Where's the accountability for the person who reported Pete to CPS? Where's the accountability for Loomer? Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. * Go back to 2024. Vance and Trump invented a lie about immigrants in Ohio eating people's pets, and millions swallowed it whole because it flattered the ugliest corner of the internet. Vance went on national television that weekend and admitted out loud that he'll invent stories to jerk the media around. What happened to him? Nothing. The media thanked him and booked him for the next hit. The lasting legacy of that lie isn't that JD Vance is a grotesque liar -- it's a catchy TikTok song stuck in my head. That's what covering politics like sports does: Jon Ossoff gets dinged for name-dropping Trump's alleged mistress in a speech -- too far, below the belt -- while the other side fabricates a child's sexual assault to annihilate one of our most effective activists. These things are not equivalent, and pretending they are is how we got here. I'm done fighting with one hand tied behind my back, and you should be too. And before someone deliberately misunderstands me: I'm not saying we become them. I'm saying we stop pretending we're playing the same game. That's what I mean by the next version of the Democratic Party -- one willing to throw a punch, for the people it loves and the Americans the MAGA machine poisons every day. You don't beat a lie by lying harder. You beat it by refusing to reward it -- by calling bullshit bullshit, by imposing consequences, by restoring some gravity. Because a system without consequences doesn't just tolerate liars -- it selects for them. If lying costs nothing, you get more liars. If cruelty makes you famous, you get more cruelty. If shamelessness buys followers and TV contracts, you get more shameless people chasing power. And if decency means your kids get threatened and your life gets turned upside down because someone with an internet connection made something up, decent people decide it isn't worth it. That's how you get the Tate brothers, George Santos, Donald Trump. What kind of person thrives where shame is a disadvantage and shamelessness is a strategy? So how do we fix it? There's no one neat policy -- government, courts, media, platforms, parties, and you all have a role. But the principle is the same: consequences again. If Dean can find whoever did this, he should sue them for everything they own, and the platforms that spread it should pay too. When you destroy a life with a lie, that lie should cost you something. I hope Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings and Fox News for the lies they've told about him. I've been thinking hard about my own options against Laura Loomer, and it's a hard road -- which tells you exactly where the burden sits. Six weeks ago I told you this is how they pick us off. This is the other half: this is how the worst people replace them. It's how you get Trump. A system without gravity created the conditions for him, and getting rid of him won't be enough, because the incentives that produced him will still be there, waiting for the next guy. Nothing changes until there are consequences again. Nothing changes until gravity comes back. In case you missed it: Tim Walz just signed an executive order to protect the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness from mining.

After Trump moved to open the door to mining in the Boundary Waters watershed, Tim took action to protect this fragile ecosystem from irreversible pollution — because places like this should be preserved for generations, not handed over to mining companies for profit.

subject: Morning meeting notes
body:
The biggest thing. The polling. The immediate need.
| | | | |
---
Hi Peter, I wanted to share a few critical updates with you coming out of a meeting I had with my campaign team.
* **The biggest thing:** The Senate GOP’s top super PAC is currently spending more in North Carolina than almost any other battleground state in the country. They recently went live with a $17 million ad buy against me – moving up their start date from September to July – because they’re seeing our momentum and panicking.
* **The polling:** With false attacks against me hitting the airwaves and as more voters get to know my opponent, Republican Michael Whatley, my narrow lead in this race has been cut to about 4 points. The polls are tightening and will continue to do so the closer we get to Election Day.
* **The immediate need:** Right now, what we need most is a surge of grassroots support from people like you so we can fight back against the GOP with new ads of our own. **We have to reach as many voters as possible with our message, as quickly as possible.**

[**_That’s what it’s going to take to win this race, so please: Will you chip in $5 or any amount today to help me respond to the GOP’s false attack ads, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1138&amount=5&t=2&akid=2845%2E124072%2EX-dohR)
Thanks so much, Peter.
Roy Cooper

It hurts all of us — because that means fewer medical breakthroughs, less climate research, slower progress on cancer treatments, degraded pandemic preparedness, and more. As a microbiologist and educator, take it from me: Science only works when it is allowed to be independent, transparent, and guided by evidence — not politics. But what we’re seeing now is a systematic effort to replace expertise with loyalty, and it’s happening at the highest levels of government. This is exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because we need leaders who will defend science and protect vital institutions like the NSF. = = When we let science lead, people thrive. Let’s put facts back in charge — and build a Congress that reflects reason, reality, and hope. | Peter,
My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday's primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.
I want to share with you why I made the decision to run - and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you're ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Jamie Davis:
---
| [CONTRIBUTE](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001MqcKX5M8hv65vXo7W-guQdLeCbYMPMdjgOiUMhXNETuqeZRdca9AtvSmFTRUL3Hz8B2_2_Z13AhzitNSKm1fm0UMYppHqYuRQlab3FRDQzd43LBFGEmHdYmne1b8DqeBamjsRY-wPkHX3t03bECauBF3Jf9izlQOExypN6Sx67UwwncRPoHelY9vsVoYYUb4UhOkL0hoXDxoaESUIYxZt9bxaAiNL-Xo&c=Bmy-PbwijbqQ7d2holBtO5NMSTSKpxU-8jCEw8V3qyA4_0Xog9TgVw==&ch=5HfG6Gtz-aKdnuQmgjzX-4AB5E5aw8zBDRY1Ta2DdvRZZk6rBjKTLg==)
---
Now here's a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don't even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets - not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it's usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It's why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we're going to secure Alaska's future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we'll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.
So I am asking:
[Please split a contribution between Jamie Davis and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November.](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001MqcKX5M8hv65vXo7W-guQdLeCbYMPMdjgOiUMhXNETuqeZRdca9AtvSmFTRUL3HzA91NetZV6e8DdepH68-397Qysc-M7GM7TCBti_79tDV5FVZ01Gq2JocTlVWIjPaDSoTqEaRNqYkFdJA_-44ZJPZjEV0bF_fKVepAVhW3C0spHq8PEAnqmb-VLsawKCfcDFiJByStChIhufaXWCbAGT_KWUuo-H9EZ4BoxvejjlQa6B3HqZWV_Q==&c=Bmy-PbwijbqQ7d2holBtO5NMSTSKpxU-8jCEw8V3qyA4_0Xog9TgVw==&ch=5HfG6Gtz-aKdnuQmgjzX-4AB5E5aw8zBDRY1Ta2DdvRZZk6rBjKTLg==)

| | Across the country, tech companies are gunning to build data centers on whatever land they can get their hands on. These facilities use as much power as 100,000 homes and take enormous amounts of water to cool. **For the parts of Oregon and our country that are already drought-prone, that's a strain on our resources we cannot afford.** Meanwhile, the demand data centers are putting on our energy grids are driving up costs for everyone else. Utility bills have skyrocketed in the last year thanks to Republican policies that are gutting new energy projects and allowing data centers to gobble up energy from the grid. But even with those insane costs, they're being built all over the country as fast as possible, including in Oregon. **Working folks shouldn't be footing the bill to subsidize the richest companies in the world.** That's why I've unveiled a new proposal that will ensure that data centers start paying for the disruptions they cause to our communities by making them pay their fair share. These taxes would help offset the costs that communities have been stuck paying. **While we prioritize innovation and remaining competitive in global markets, we must ensure that companies are paying their share of the bill, and my plan is the way to do it.** Onward, _Ron_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Ron Wyden instantly:

clean_body: | | | | Across the country, tech companies are gunning to build data centers on whatever land they can get their hands on. These facilities use as much power as 100,000 homes and take enormous amounts of water to cool. For the parts of Oregon and our country that are already drought-prone, that's a strain on our resources we cannot afford. Meanwhile, the demand data centers are putting on our energy grids are driving up costs for everyone else. Utility bills have skyrocketed in the last year thanks to Republican policies that are gutting new energy projects and allowing data centers to gobble up energy from the grid. But even with those insane costs, they're being built all over the country as fast as possible, including in Oregon. Working folks shouldn't be footing the bill to subsidize the richest companies in the world. That's why I've unveiled a new proposal that will ensure that data centers start paying for the disruptions they cause to our communities by making them pay their fair share. These taxes would help offset the costs that communities have been stuck paying. While we prioritize innovation and remaining competitive in global markets, we must ensure that companies are paying their share of the bill, and my plan is the way to do it. **Evaluating Voter Verification Systems Two Decades Later**
In the two decades since Congress passed the Help America Vote Act of 2002, the machinery of American election integrity has undergone a profound technological transformation. What began as a mandate for statewide voter databases and basic identity verification has evolved into a complex ecosystem of real-time data matching, involving the Social Security Administration's Help America Vote Verification (HAVV) system and, increasingly, the Department of Homeland Security's Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program. A close examination of how these tools have performed since the problematic 2005 era--when a GAO report documented Texas officials discovering an attempt to register using 42 deceased individuals' names--reveals a mixed record of progress, persistent limitations, and urgent questions about how states should deploy verification technology before future elections
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/df15e060-b730-4426-9d9d-e09c3cf1ab21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**HAVV: The Data Backbone**
SSA's HAVV system remains the most established tool in the verification arsenal. When a voter registration applicant lacks a driver's license, election officials submit the individual's name, date of birth, and the last four digits of their Social Security Number to SSA. The system returns one of several verification codes, including Code 6, indicating that the data matched SSA records but that the individual is flagged as deceased. This is a critical gatekeeping function: a deceased match means the registration should be halted pending further review.
The HAVV system has improved measurably since 2005. Transaction volumes are now published weekly at ssa.gov/data/havv, providing a degree of transparency that was absent in the early years. States have moved from batch processing to more routine electronic verification. The AAMVA documentation confirms that HAVV returns granular result codes--allowing officials to distinguish between a simple name mismatch, a non-existent SSN, and a deceased individual. In theory, this precision should prevent the kind of undetected fraud that the 2005 Texas case exemplified.
Yet HAVV is not a cure-all. The system only verifies what states submit; it cannot detect registrations that use false information never sent to SSA. Moreover, because HAVV is triggered primarily when applicants lack driver's licenses, it captures only a subset of the registration stream. And while the system flags potential deceased matches, public weekly data aggregates transactions without publishing state-by-state counts of Code 6 results, meaning outside observers cannot independently audit whether deceased-flag rates are anomalous in specific jurisdictions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3aa59d7-e9c1-4747-b79a-5c8321f4057d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**SAVE: The Controversial Expansion**
If HAVV represents the steady evolution of identity verification, SAVE represents a more volatile and politically charged expansion into citizenship verification. Originally designed to verify benefit eligibility for immigrants, SAVE was dramatically repurposed beginning in 2025 to audit voter rolls for alleged non-citizen registrations. This expansion has proven deeply problematic.
Texas's experience is instructive. In April 2026, former Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson informed USCIS that her office had identified 2,724 potential non-citizens through SAVE--but emphasized that county-level investigations were ongoing and that the data required careful review. Votebeat Texas subsequently reported that SAVE was "mistakenly flagging voters as noncitizens," and the Brennan Center for Justice warned that the tool's known inaccuracies posed severe risks of wrongful disenfranchisement. Put simply, SAVE's error rate is high enough that officials in Texas--hardly a jurisdiction known for lax election oversight--publicly questioned its reliability.
The distinction between HAVV and SAVE is crucial here. HAVV checks identity and life status against SSA records with relatively straightforward matching logic. SAVE, by contrast, attempts to adjudicate citizenship status using DHS databases that were never designed for real-time voter roll maintenance. Data lags, naturalization record delays, and inconsistent state-to-federal data sharing mean SAVE routinely flags naturalized U.S. citizens as aliens. Where HAVV provides clarity, SAVE too often creates confusion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1d976226-33ce-4af4-a6de-c6cf8266c11e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The Missouri Question**
Against this backdrop, the approaching November election demands rigorous scrutiny of how states are using these tools. Missouri has reportedly utilized verification systems in ways that generated striking figures--in one reportedly cited instance, tens of thousands of registrations flagged for verification concerns in a single week. Whether these numbers reflect HAVV deceased matches, SAVE citizenship flags, or some combination of systems, the scale alone underscores the importance of process integrity.
Missouri could learn from both Texas's caution and California's model. Texas officials recognized that raw SAVE hits require human review and county-level confirmation before any removal action; California, meanwhile, runs continuous cross-checks between its VoteCal system and state death records from the Department of Public Health, catching discrepancies before they propagate into disputed registrations. Missouri should adopt a similarly multi-layered approach: using HAVV for identity verification, treating SAVE data as a leads list rather than an execution order, and mandating secondary confirmation--such as contact with the voter or cross-reference with vital records--before canceling any registration.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c297cbd-c035-4c81-9e72-df9718189938?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Recommendations for November**
With election integrity justifiably a vital concern, states preparing for November should remember three lessons from the post-2005 era. First, verification tools are only as good as the processes surrounding them. An automated flag from HAVV or SAVE should trigger due process, not automatic cancellation. Second, transparency matters. If Missouri or any state is sitting on thousands of flagged registrations, the public deserves clarity about what systems generated those flags and what error rates those systems carry. Third, training remains essential. The 2005 Texas case involved a human or systemic failure that allowed fraudulent registrations to reach the point of submission; modern technology should reduce that risk, but only if local officials understand the difference between a HAVV mismatch and a SAVE false positive.
The system is working better than it did in 2005, but "better" does not mean "flawless." HAVV has become a reliable identity-verification backbone, while SAVE remains a troubled tool whose misuse could disenfranchise eligible voters. As November approaches, states would do well to rely more heavily on the former while treating the latter with far greater skepticism--ensuring that the pursuit of election integrity does not come at the cost of legitimate voters' constitutional rights.

body:
The CHIPS Act turns four this month. Here’s what I want to know.
---
| | Hey Peter,

Four years ago this month, we passed the CHIPS and Science Act.

For two decades, this country invented the technology and then let someone else build it. We designed the chips here and manufactured them 7,000 miles away. Then a pandemic hit, supply chains snapped, and the price of a used car told every American what that dependence actually cost us.

**San Diego is exactly the kind of place that vote was written for. Wireless, biotech, defense, clean energy - our economy runs on research that turns into products that turn into careers. CHIPS put federal muscle behind the research pipeline and behind building things on American soil again.**

But a law is only as good as what gets built. So I want to hear from you:

**[WHAT SHOULD WE BE BUILDING IN SAN DIEGO?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137529468/641094419/1263909100?refcode2=SP_EM_SV_180DO_260813_1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NjM1NjA5My1lZjliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jOJyubkljc_lLyqQMia43v7HmIoB4qARbeWfBJAltus=&emci=43356093-ef9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=46356093-ef9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=5258741)**

→ Advanced manufacturing jobs that don't require a four-year degree
→ Research and STEM funding that keeps our universities and startups here
→ Clean energy - and the grid to actually connect it
→ All of it, and faster

I ask because the follow-through is the whole ballgame, and it is under real threat. Federal research funding is being cut. Permits still take a decade. _If we lose the House, the follow-through stops._

Scott

clean_body: The CHIPS Act turns four this month. Here’s what I want to know. | | Hey Peter, Four years ago this month, we passed the CHIPS and Science Act. For two decades, this country invented the technology and then let someone else build it. We designed the chips here and manufactured them 7,000 miles away. Then a pandemic hit, supply chains snapped, and the price of a used car told every American what that dependence actually cost us. San Diego is exactly the kind of place that vote was written for. Wireless, biotech, defense, clean energy - our economy runs on research that turns into products that turn into careers. CHIPS put federal muscle behind the research pipeline and behind building things on American soil again. But a law is only as good as what gets built. So I want to hear from you: → Advanced manufacturing jobs that don't require a four-year degree → Research and STEM funding that keeps our universities and startups here → Clean energy - and the grid to actually connect it → All of it, and faster I ask because the follow-through is the whole ballgame, and it is under real threat. Federal research funding is being cut. Permits still take a decade. If we lose the House, the follow-through stops. | | Tell me where you think we should build, and I will bring it back to Washington with me. Last year, at least 88 of the biggest corporations in America paid zero in federal corporate income taxes last year — even while posting healthy pretax profits here in the U.S. _**That didn’t happen by accident.**_ It’s the predictable result when politicians cut taxes for big companies and then let the people who profit from those cuts write the rules. Meanwhile, the same interests pushing for tax giveaways are also the ones pouring money into political campaigns and lobbying for loopholes that benefit them. My GOP opponent, Rob Bresnahan, accepts corporate donations from companies like these and continues to sell out NEPA anytime he can pad his portfolio. This is how corporate money in politics works: it buys influence, it shapes policy, and it shields profits from public accountability. You can see the consequences clearly — promises about protecting healthcare or restoring fairness rings hollow when the policies coming out of DC tilt toward special interests instead of families. body:
Let the general election begin!
| | | | | [](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FodqvwF9cbMWwWUbWxyNyumXJF9b_Z5dNxoIklSzZU-uv1Wlb9e8AWecEfF_AKhHbIPOKhD5hEE_EGTpHQQvbmuTiStW6cXqz1zgxJgIyQis_FxvwwBFkv3-p2g5z5p3BK4WwHXvB-RwmCmV_y73iBR1BgFtGw2YpQ67DrsLMP8jnmdNKYt9Cy8RpcrqkGLuAgjet7O0FXxp94Z2p0XcgI_1CAuNC93RCTls9iB4eBY=&c=V9M58X5uN7DCos1GQIKVKia9gRNFDD0zw7Csb-1o3JIopTWE6CAsdw==&ch=Gu7pI42oncAQ2hp0tx1bB6fOTwfI83-pOffmmNqaZOgKWqPYEHlcpA==)
---

Peter, My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday's primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.
I want to share with you why I made the decision to run - and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you're ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and the Nebraska Democrats:

---
| [CONTRIBUTE](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FodqvwF9cbMWwWUbWxyNyumXJF9b_Z5dNxoIklSzZU-uv1Wlb9e8AWecEfF_AKhHbIPOKhD5hEE_EGTpHQQvbmuTiStW6cXqz1zgxJgIyQis_FxvwwBFkv3-p2g5z5p3BK4WwHXvB-RwmCmV_y73iBR1BgFtGw2YpQ67DrsLMP8jnmdNKYt9Cy8RpcrqkGLuAgjet7O0FXxp94Z2p0XcgC-SIh1G5gNSbnObobKX_IU=&c=V9M58X5uN7DCos1GQIKVKia9gRNFDD0zw7Csb-1o3JIopTWE6CAsdw==&ch=Gu7pI42oncAQ2hp0tx1bB6fOTwfI83-pOffmmNqaZOgKWqPYEHlcpA==)
---
Now here's a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don't even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets - not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it's usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It's why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we're going to secure Alaska's future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we'll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.
So I am asking:
[Please split a contribution between the Nebraska Democratic Party and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November.](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FodqvwF9cbMWwWUbWxyNyumXJF9b_Z5dNxoIklSzZU-uv1Wlb9e8AWecEfF_AKhHt_VZ3Y6gD7A8OGDSzDQf8BebGQDEGwkL_pPnAVMNKrHt0_7Ejd79bppx25kZ12u-2_bzlsXjELczZbxT88R6wnD_Jb4h4D0HBMUS5VYXkXlUhnz1IANc6uQiAEOBg5fpZVT8DnOCaf2rMCyip7MkKgc97Df9sRffiMKoW5yl8NOL2e_7Jnp4KjBvnFJOiw6p&c=V9M58X5uN7DCos1GQIKVKia9gRNFDD0zw7Csb-1o3JIopTWE6CAsdw==&ch=Gu7pI42oncAQ2hp0tx1bB6fOTwfI83-pOffmmNqaZOgKWqPYEHlcpA==)

But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you're ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and the Nebraska Democrats: | == Now here's a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don't even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets - not ours. And when they actually work together on something, it's usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It's why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home. My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we're going to secure Alaska's future, we need another priority: fighting corruption. I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we'll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.
