|
Peter,
Donald Trump is throwing everything at the wall right now to try and manufacture pretext that will allow him to rig the upcoming midterms. This most recent attempt might be his most desperate, insane scheme yet.
On "Truth" Social, Trump announced that the U.S. Census Bureau, the agency responsible for the decennial census used for congressional apportionment, was tasked with checking voter records against citizenship records from the 2020 election--a mission far outside the intended scope of the agency.
Trump claimed that the Census Bureau has already proved that he actually won the 2020 election, claiming that the Bureau has found over 24,000 Noncitizens who voted illegally in the 2020 election.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001PB6JD15kDsuO4iWyX74fFf_X8dV6GxDnOtI32Bc2tL42N6HDsT0Ei07EtFiQM_Q3Pr60O9_ycxtTFQUzZas3FUB8iHOW2sHxaQJPjFIueBFfn86qJ8VtwPlKNQh9cNEPM0x6peSREWJz8MYBt9W5eqcaCzBryGA4rSC97Pu6aHRGWG8M39fWL0VjXk365iafrtxY10VBuy0mA_nQ0XVfaNv8fe2KSotsfe35qdbYvYA=&c=HEZhHkipZKjpYqHdkoIqLKMOpxe661jq8VLQpOh4K8k_UdxNkT5HqA==&ch=KhUC8FlyZYZefcqG_EL2Ymf_2SHu-MQsj3_9cIpcbwXfTcCYlNFzDw==)
---
Uh huh, sure.
But this latest scam isn't simply about protecting Trump's fragile ego by providing manufactured data to "prove" he didn't actually lose the 2020 election, it is also about manufacturing pretext to challenge November's midterms results.
Weeks ago, when Trump gave his primetime national address on elections, Trump made a dubious claim that the Department of Homeland Security found more than 250,000 noncitizens registered to vote in just four states.
But nobody from the Trump administration can explain where those numbers came from. NPR reported that multiple state officials warned these completely made-up numbers could be used by the Trump administration to justify federal law enforcement interference in counting votes this November.

Peter -
My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday’s primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.
I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Heartland Patriots:
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107782?refcode=em20260819-10819&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10819%2E614464%2Et-32iU)**
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
**[Please split a contribution between Heartland Patriots and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. Peter - My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday’s primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska. I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together. But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Heartland Patriots: Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets – not ours. And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home. My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption. I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. The scale of Trump's grifting during his second term has exceeded what many of us feared, and every American should know about it.
Here are what I consider to be Trump’s 10 worst grifts so far:
10\. Since his re-election, the Trump family has made at least **$23 million** licensing the Trump name overseas. A hotel in Oman, towers in India, golf courses outside Riyadh and Doha — all requiring the cooperation of foreign governments who want something in return. This has made Americans less safe since U.S. foreign policy is for sale.
9\. Trump extorted American media companies for **$36 million.** In one of the worst attacks on the free press our nation has ever seen, Trump used the leverage afforded to him by the presidency to approve mergers so he could line his own pockets. This will cost people their jobs and force consumers to pay more for fewer choices on streaming services.
8\. Social media companies and tech have capitulated to Trump, even after he used their platforms to encourage violence and spread lies. Companies like Meta, Youtube, and Twitter (now Elon Musk’s X) have handed over more than **$60 million** to Trump and his pet causes.
7\. Jeff Bezos's Amazon gave Melania Trump a **$40 million** contract for her failed film in the hopes of getting huge government contracts and access to the president. So taxpayers pay more for cloud computing and may get an inferior product.
6\. The $TRUMP memecoin, launched just 24 hours before his inauguration, netted the president more than **$600 million.** His 810,000+ buyers, mostly his own supporters, lost a combined $2 billion.
5\. The president’s ballroom was supposed to cost taxpayers nothing. Now this gold-gilded vanity project is costing taxpayers **$300 million** and giving donors a leg up on massive government contracts.
4\. Trump was gifted a **$400 million** luxury jet by the government of Qatar, becoming his new Air Force One. Taxpayers have to pay up to a billion in security upgrades and when Trump is done with the presidency — he and his museum get to keep it!
3\. Nine wealthy law firms pledged nearly **$1 billion** in "pro bono services" to avoid retaliation by this White House — an arrangement negotiated not by a government official, but by Trump's personal legal team. It means you may find it hard to get representation if your interests are not aligned with Trump.
2\. Ever heard of World Liberty Financial? The Trump family owns roughly 75% of it. Token sales alone have earned them well over a billion dollars, and they collect stablecoin interest worth **$1.5 billion** and counting. Much of the money comes from Gulf countries which may further embroil the U.S. in their affairs.
1\. Trump has tried to steal **$1.776 billion** in taxpayer dollars to go to January 6th rioters, aggrieved right-wingers, and those who feel the DOJ targeted them. He also carved out a **$100 million** deal for himself and his kids with the IRS.
All in all, the cost of these grifts totals up to **$6 billion.** _And that’s just the top ten._
The first step to stopping this corruption is to expose it. The second step is to communicate to the American people how this corruption affects their lives and costs. The final step is to elect a Democratic majority that can help put an end to it.

# Three readers just put $45,000 behind our Gaza coverage
### Every dollar goes directly to the Palestinian journalists reporting from the ground in Gaza
| | | [Drop Site News](https://substack.com/@dropsitenews)
---
| Aug 19
---
| [](https://substack.com/@dropsitenews)
---
Over the past few weeks, three Drop Site readers came to us independently with the same idea. They wanted to know one thing: if they committed real money to our Gaza reporting, would our community match it.
Together, they've pledged $45,000 to fund and expand our reporting on the ground in Gaza and our investigations into Israel's ongoing assault on the Palestinian people. That reporting is done by Palestinian journalists and correspondents who have kept working through two years of a genocide that has killed more of their colleagues than any conflict in modern history. It was a significant investment they wanted to see doubled by the community that believes in and depends on this reporting. That money only turns into support for the brave journalists actually doing this work if the rest of us meet them there.
Here's the deal: if we raise $45,000 from readers like you, every one of those dollars gets matched, we'll have **$90,000 dedicated entirely to our Gaza coverage.** Your $25 becomes $50. Your $50 becomes $100. Your $100 becomes $200.
[Will you help us raise $45,000 in matching funds? If we reach our goal by August 24th, every gift will be doubled.](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Double My Gift Now](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **Here 's why this matters right now**
For two years, Western outlets have taken Israel's unverified claims, that a murdered journalist was secretly a militant, that a strike on a hospital or a refugee camp was justified, and repeated them as fact, giving Israel's military the space to launder each atrocity into something defensible. Legacy media never covered this story honestly. Now it isn't even covering it at all. One analysis of US news coverage found that mentions of Gaza across major outlets fell to just 1.5% of their coverage in the months after the supposed "ceasefire," less than two-thirds of what it was before the agreement, and the lowest sustained level of coverage since October 2023. The same newsrooms that laundered this genocide for two years have simply moved on from it, the moment Trump declared the story finished.
It isn't finished. Israel has killed more than 1,280 Palestinians since that so-called "ceasefire" began, including over 300 children. Homes are still being seized and demolished in the West Bank. Settlers are murdering Palestinians in broad daylight, under military protection, while cancer patients in Gaza die at two to three times the prewar rate because the hospitals that could treat them were targeted and destroyed.
The gap between what corporate media launders or flatly ignores and what actually is happening, is the reason Drop Site exists. Right now, you have the opportunity to help close that gap.
[Will you help us turn $45,000 into $90,000 to directly fund our Gaza reporting?](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Yes, I'll help unlock the full $90,000](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **Our promise**
Two years ago, we launched this newsroom because we watched outlet after outlet either look away from what was happening in Gaza or sanitize it beyond recognition. We made a promise when we started: we would cover this with the depth, consistency, and honesty it demands, for as long as it takes, without asking permission from advertisers, foundations, or anyone else who might prefer we look away too.
Here's what that promise actually looks like in practice: our reporting you read from inside Gaza is done by Palestinian journalists who live there, who have kept working and kept documenting through two years of a genocide that has killed more of their colleagues than any conflict in modern history. That is one of the most heroic acts of journalism in history, done under conditions almost no one reading (or writing) this could imagine. A significant share of our budget goes directly to paying these journalists and correspondents for that work. **When you give to this campaign, you are funding the people risking everything, every day, to make sure this story doesn 't disappear.**
$90,000 dedicated specifically to this work would let us do more of it, and do it faster: more support for the Palestinian journalists and correspondents already doing this reporting on the ground, more capacity to verify what's happening as the media blackout deepens, more resources for the people risking everything to get us the truth.
[Support Drop Site's Gaza Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **This is reader-funded journalism, which means this is on us**
We don't have a billionaire owner who can write a $90,000 check and call it done. We're funded by readers who decide, one gift at a time, that this coverage is worth keeping alive. That takes more work than cashing a corporate check, but it also means nobody can pull our funding because they didn't like a headline. Nobody can influence or shape our coverage or what or who we report on. We answer to you and nobody else.
Three generous supporters already stepped up in a big way. Now we need the rest of the community to meet them, not with one huge gift, but with thousands of readers giving what they can. [Every gift gets matched dollar for dollar until we hit $45,000, and every dollar of it goes directly to our Gaza reporting, which means it goes directly to the Palestinian journalists doing that reporting.](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Double my gift for Gaza reporting ->](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We built Drop Site because the public deserved better than a media industry that has been complicit in the dehumanization of Palestinians and served as a conveyor belt for Israeli propaganda instead of the truth. Help us prove that promise still means something.
Thank you for being here, and for making this kind of journalism possible.
Jeremy, Ryan and the Drop Site team
_[Every gift to Drop Site News is tax-deductible](https://substack.com/redirect/e4c3be6e-9dd6-41fa-8f86-0247a02768e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This campaign runs until August 24th or until we hit our $45,000 match goal, whichever comes first._
(C) 2026 Drop Site News, Inc.

Ste B2 #1034, Washington, DC 20009

Friend,
During certain weekends, I go silent.
No calls from me. No events with me. No meetings with me. No fundraisers with me.
Why? Because I'm an officer in the Army National Guard. And when I'm on duty, I am required to stop campaigning. Period. I even have to brief my team in advance -- pick one person, hand them the keys, and hope they get it right.
I joined the Guard at 35. Older than most. Older than my drill sergeants. The oldest guy in my bootcamp class -- and proud of it.
Today, I serve as a public defender for our soldiers. Because every soldier deserves a real defense. Every soldier deserves the rule of law. No exceptions.
I'm the first-generation son of two immigrants. This country gave my family a shot at the American Dream. Wearing this uniform is how I do my part. Nothing flashy. Just duty.
---

| | | Peter -

My name is Mary Peltola, and after yesterday’s primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.

I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.

**[But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Equal Opportunity Now:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137544131/641128382/916216164?amount=25&refcode=260819_peltolavictorysplit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMmNmNGI0Zi0wNzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=o-oYs4TZxAk2IfGSvRKIT6DYB8HwhlrJRGuV4zNHjTg=)**

Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**

So I am asking:

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets – not ours. And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home. ### **Help us defeat the mainstream media, promote capitalism and American exceptionalism.**
### **[Support The Capitalist, become a paid subscriber today:](https://substack.com/redirect/3e55a7c6-48ed-4e8b-9193-731bce18da80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Subscribe Here](https://substack.com/redirect/3e55a7c6-48ed-4e8b-9193-731bce18da80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
This past weekend I attended my first DSA meeting, held in a cavernous church basement that was littered with dozens of "F-ck ICE!" and "No Trump, No KKK, No Fascist USA" picket signs. The meeting was for people who were interested in joining the DSA; Called "DSA 101", it was an introductory course led by a public school teacher. In the fifteen minutes between my arrival and the event's start time, about twenty-five white people trickled into the room.
The instructor started the class by lamenting the recent loss of DSA gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong. Almost everyone in the room had Hong buttons pinned to their bags or shirts. One woman was using a soda coozie with a Hong quote printed on it: "If you need me I'll be balls deep in bourbon." The instructor blamed Hong's loss on the consolidation of the Democrat party around the "centrist, moderate" David Crowley and his annoyance with current Democrat Governor Tony Evers' endorsement of Crowley. He then read a quote from a German Marxist, Bertolt Brecht: "The persecutors are wicked simply because they persecute. The persecuted suffer because of their goodness."
The leader then began outlining the differences between socialism and capitalism, placing particular emphasis on the working class. The group instructor, who also claims to run and edit a local socialist magazine, asked the group to define the working class. The next few minutes produced a brief discussion on who was included in the working class: Workers, but not business owners (Who were, of course, stealing labor). Wage earners, but not the police. Children, but also not children. All people, but not everybody, because as one ambiguously gendered individual stated, "We have to keep in mind that anyone could become disabled at any point." Everyone enthusiastically nodded in agreement. "Workers Deserve More" was the three-word summary used to explain the difference between capitalism and socialism.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8f471c25-c41e-4fbb-a1b5-19f09cf0ce27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## _" I just think that socialists have an amazing opportunity to really take advantage of our current moment..." _
Said the 30-something year old woman sitting next to me at the DSA meeting. Everyone else at the table, including three other millennial women and two gentlemen who were late-Gen Xers, nodded in agreement. _**" Now more than ever, people need what socialism has to offer."**_
* * *

# **[If the House Flips, Don't Let Your 401(k) Take the Hit](https://substack.com/redirect/bfd71e6e-649b-4996-b484-3ffcd3d7016e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bfd71e6e-649b-4996-b484-3ffcd3d7016e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Move your hard-earned savings out of paper risk before ballots are cast.**
If you are 5 to 10 years from retirement, this election season is not background noise. It is a reminder to take a serious look at the retirement savings you've accumulated and put some protective measures in place.
If the Democrats manage to flip the House and/or Senate, it breaks the current legislative balance. The mainstream media may call it a victory for oversight, but history shows what this shift could mean for your savings...
Election fueled volatility that could leave soon-to-be retirees with losses in their 401(k)'s. Prolonged budget battles that can rattle consumer confidence and corporate earnings. A Democratic pushback against President Trump's economic growth plan.
For those closing in on your retirement date, it doesn't take a major market crash to threaten everything you've worked for.
A sudden shift in power and the volatility of an election cycle is just enough to shave years worth of comfort from the retirement budget you're planning for.
Do not let one election cycle break your nest egg when you're so close to the finish line.
**[Download our 2026 Wealth Preservation Guide Now!](https://substack.com/redirect/bfd71e6e-649b-4996-b484-3ffcd3d7016e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Download HERE](https://substack.com/redirect/bfd71e6e-649b-4996-b484-3ffcd3d7016e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
The instructor walked the group through some of the DSA's core principles: Expanded public resources, health care for all (Including gender affirming care and access to abortion), housing for all, finishing reconstruction by ending white supremacy, ending mass incarceration, and abolishing the police, whom were described as "An unaccountable, racist, oppressive institution." Feminism was also described as a core tenant of the DSA, describing women as constituting a majority of the working class, and stating that all forms of housework were oppressive. Springing from this was a call to "End patriarchal domination and give full equality for women and gender non-conforming people, and absolute support for trans rights." Finally, he mentioned the Green New Deal. During a small group discussion where we were asked to say which of these social causes we were most passionate about, the majority of women in my circle noted their particular passion for "climate justice." A young man wearing a pride tank top walking by overheard this and chimed in, "Soooooo true, Comrade!"
The instructor then explained how socialism is an inherently international movement. He criticized the "American military industrial complex," mentioned the need to free Palestine, demanded that Israeli leaders be "prosecuted for genocide," and bemoaned that America had punished Cuba with sanctions as "punishment" for being a communist country.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6b5dfba4-8f02-4118-a2ff-089702970bc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The last major point he hit on, of course, was abolishing ICE. At the very mention of ICE, attendees started booing and yelling "F-ck them!", while the public school teacher at the front of the room smiled and laughed. "I don't care to live in a state where people can be abused and murdered by Stephen Miller's lunatic Gestapo," He said, before going on to explain that "ICE is a tool of American imperialism, racism, and violence... It is built to oppress, terrorize, and murder people. Socialism is not a fan of immigration enforcement writ large." He blamed all immigration issues on American imperialism.
* * *
* * *
### Support The Capitalist by getting the SubStack App
[Get the App](https://substack.com/redirect/300a6c8d-ebb5-43bc-8030-c90e6c684576?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
Around the end of the session, the instructor said the quiet part out loud: "[ICE] is not something that has existed since the constitution, although the constitution is not that great in my opinion." He laughed the comment off and mumbled something along the lines of "Don't tell my job that I said that." The other attendees cried out in agreement, barking about how it was "Old" and a "Living document."
Walking away from the event, I realized that the general consensus among everyone involved was that they thought of themselves as victims. The instructor encouraged the idea that all of their problems were caused by the capitalist ruling class. Their individual problems would be solved by handing over their autonomy to the state. The DSA is not simply coalescing around empathy, but around a seething hatred for others. The socialists cosplaying as "social justice warriors" are gravitating to a much more dangerous philosophy: Jealousy.

A Democratic pushback against President Trump's economic growth plan. For those closing in on your retirement date, it doesn't take a major market crash to threaten everything you've worked for. A sudden shift in power and the volatility of an election cycle is just enough to shave years worth of comfort from the retirement budget you're planning for. Do not let one election cycle break your nest egg when you're so close to the finish line. The instructor walked the group through some of the DSA's core principles: Expanded public resources, health care for all (Including gender affirming care and access to abortion), housing for all, finishing reconstruction by ending white supremacy, ending mass incarceration, and abolishing the police, whom were described as "An unaccountable, racist, oppressive institution." Feminism was also described as a core tenant of the DSA, describing women as constituting a majority of the working class, and stating that all forms of housework were oppressive. Springing from this was a call to "End patriarchal domination and give full equality for women and gender non-conforming people, and absolute support for trans rights." Finally, he mentioned the Green New Deal. During a small group discussion where we were asked to say which of these social causes we were most passionate about, the majority of women in my circle noted their particular passion for "climate justice." A young man wearing a pride tank top walking by overheard this and chimed in, "Soooooo true, Comrade!" The instructor then explained how socialism is an inherently international movement. He criticized the "American military industrial complex," mentioned the need to free Palestine, demanded that Israeli leaders be "prosecuted for genocide," and bemoaned that America had punished Cuba with sanctions as "punishment" for being a communist country. The last major point he hit on, of course, was abolishing ICE. At the very mention of ICE, attendees started booing and yelling "F-ck them!", while the public school teacher at the front of the room smiled and laughed. "I don't care to live in a state where people can be abused and murdered by Stephen Miller's lunatic Gestapo," He said, before going on to explain that "ICE is a tool of American imperialism, racism, and violence... It is built to oppress, terrorize, and murder people. Socialism is not a fan of immigration enforcement writ large." He blamed all immigration issues on American imperialism. Support The Capitalist by getting the SubStack App Around the end of the session, the instructor said the quiet part out loud: "[ICE] is not something that has existed since the constitution, although the constitution is not that great in my opinion." He laughed the comment off and mumbled something along the lines of "Don't tell my job that I said that." The other attendees cried out in agreement, barking about how it was "Old" and a "Living document." Walking away from the event, I realized that the general consensus among everyone involved was that they thought of themselves as victims. The instructor encouraged the idea that all of their problems were caused by the capitalist ruling class. Their individual problems would be solved by handing over their autonomy to the state. The DSA is not simply coalescing around empathy, but around a seething hatred for others. The socialists cosplaying as "social justice warriors" are gravitating to a much more dangerous philosophy: Jealousy. Let us know your thoughts. * | A guest post by| , conservative, cookie baker. | Wednesday, August 19, 2026| Iran Truce Lapses, Hormuz On Edge

5-minute read · 4 stories
Lead Story · Foreign PolicyCEASEFIRE WITH IRAN LAPSES AS STRAIT OF HORMUZ STANDOFF DEEPENSWhat's Happening
* The **60-day U.S.–Iran negotiating window ended Monday, Aug. 17** , with no agreement to end the war or reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
* The United Arab Emirates said Iran fired two ballistic missiles toward the country Tuesday — one falling outside its territorial waters, the second inside them. Iran's foreign ministry denied launching them.
* A commercial vessel transiting the strait was struck by an "unknown projectile," killing one crew member, the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center reported.

The Situation
* Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the strait will stay closed until Washington meets its commitments under the expired framework.
* President Trump has floated declaring the Strait of Hormuz U.S. territory and warned he would strike Oman if it interfered in negotiations.
* Brent crude climbed back above **$90 a barrel** , up roughly 2–3% over the prior 24 hours as traders priced in the risk to global oil flows.

The PerspectiveA world that depends on the Strait of Hormuz cannot let Tehran treat it as a hostage. The administration is right to keep maximum pressure on a regime that walked away from the table rather than give up its leverage, and right to remind allies like Oman that neutrality cannot mean shielding an aggressor. Talk of annexing the strait is bluster that gets ahead of the facts on the ground, and the death of a merchant sailor is a sober reminder that the cost of this standoff is measured in lives, not just barrels. Peace is worth pursuing — but not a peace that hands Iran a veto over the world's energy lifeline.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_N8M2yF9-VjcaxkG0L0zQSWtmRRgk4AXR96ZbyGrUWgYoy_b6HaJbTQpl5RFd4O0c0gNTpCsCw2Pr2g1A4sxUUhzskvAVyjkr_VBHUGmesDBkY2Aqh08y3kG9hSF8RkdJ8B7mZ-EeOgK8XGvlPwXtgPDAl0h-VG-WGLfWjv1WPKdEYcheGYSJOsT4NaIfWZcA0gQae9fE8h4a4Q0UKUn3vb5QVd8t47gzQcqG9SUZ9a5VVzUyqVlcvYUDMFvF1PobF5mCFlMZrGSY25VXoQq3yHFPDd5XOqwcoiP-UCjgj-ptVraeBhgLMN_VRMBhmw2y6MDFy0lFtKCoJ4vhljMslI/4tb/YhiL3SgeS32phsXvz3f4XQ/h5/h001.fltskn6THaDb1QvZFLUWhU1UFSp0GtCREEZQJWXB2TQ)

The EconomyNEW TARIFFS ON CANADIAN GOODS SET TO HIT THIS WEEKWhat's Happening
* A fresh round of U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports is set to take effect **Wednesday** after talks between Washington and Ottawa stalled.
* The duties would cover roughly **$20 billion** in goods, including some clothing, wines, dairy products, hockey sticks and building materials such as cement and plywood.
* Canadian broadcaster CBC reported the two sides were at an impasse despite weeks of meetings.

The Situation
* Importers can pass the new duties on to shoppers, adding pressure on households already facing higher costs.
* Consumer prices are up about **3.4%** over the past year, per NBC News — up from 2.4% before the Iran war began.
* Tariffs already cost the average American household roughly $1,100 a year, according to an estimate from Yale's Budget Lab.

The PerspectiveTariffs are leverage, and used surgically they can pry open lopsided trade deals that Washington let fester for decades. But leverage has a price, and honesty requires admitting that some of that price lands on American families at the checkout counter. The right test is simple: are these duties delivering better terms and reshoring real production, or just adding a line item to the grocery bill? A deal with Canada that levels the field would vindicate the strategy. A stalemate that quietly raises prices while an election looms would not. Voters can tell the difference.[Read the full story at NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_KnXUR8YWdaXuMqU6tjDoFVp6LEQjGkSc99YMRWwWId3LW7-wFtBXSAip4yG6HZm-vFYu0tjp-wSTt9Q2g6DVY4zf6-t0nFjNm535-M57SF8ePjzzppGUUbI_JoBgb9QDwo27ko1dIvr4R7SmPkSer4votcuUKOdW6SFCFVRY5V2fM3UAfMGJxmtgwu2S69H_KMdHGsNdF6O4ybAL4C6wV7MQkYHSatQSkIzhTHoUU3FvADDR5zWOrqMe5Lb7wa4UtoNtSM8_IsHwtlMfSvQNyDBEAtSS6cJO29l1eCVUxx6DsMkb-F7Y0ddgf8z-zAqZXNMvHDLm2URi1x387IykE4/4tb/YhiL3SgeS32phsXvz3f4XQ/h6/h001.9s7Uezpecz6Km4fluMXxh_CpPWW3GH3kDB6iuKIOIE0)

The 2026 MapSULLIVAN AND PELTOLA ADVANCE IN ALASKA SENATE PRIMARYWhat's Happening
* Sen. **Dan Sullivan (R-AK)** and former Democratic Rep. **Mary Peltola** advanced from Alaska's 16-candidate nonpartisan primary Tuesday.
* With about half the vote counted, Peltola led narrowly, **45.9% to Sullivan's 45%** , according to the Associated Press.
* Under Alaska's system, the top four finishers advance to a ranked-choice general election in November.

The Situation
* The Cook Political Report rates the seat a toss-up; Democrats need to net four seats to take the Senate.
* The Senate Leadership Fund has committed roughly $17 million to the race, adding $2 million this month to defend Sullivan.
* Trump carried Alaska by 13 points in 2024, and Peltola has kept her distance from national Democrats — her campaign declined a fundraising appeal from Kamala Harris's PAC.

The PerspectiveAlaska is the kind of race that decides Senate majorities, and the early numbers should keep Republicans honest rather than complacent. Sullivan is a proven statewide winner in a state Trump carried comfortably, but Peltola has done it before, and her studied distance from Harris and the national party is a tell: even Democrats know their brand is a liability in flyover country. A primary is not a general election, and ranked-choice voting adds a wildcard that has burned the GOP here before. The lesson is to compete for every vote and let the contrast — commonsense versus a party lurching left — do the work.[Read the full story at Washington Examiner](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyXVppiSKgyDOfmQE1iA2Q6feP26i8skzhG01HhpOZ0-7EsNkq5QIHQRJRxC8FvKD5lqu8kmZvLoVIgaJ1e9VhsXd4tNZCeGNrYCj7kbDqp7cWr6gy7PB0pT-BxMgRU2z_NYV_xZEYhTr0cp4iZ8GK0jNK8pmJZx2dDbbAA0QyudGniRzBCj_mM3uICK5jXU26G9DjnKMnSN4yxinVYZcP2ruFZ1wGW6JkGp0BUb5TXiE13Q7G8mw_081fUu6PVI8GkbsGsOwRUDgT-r_cJGsjpIqTbppr6Lcccx9ovzKj4EuDh6Sss1VgwyaWC6tDHVFTLX190s5U7WizuPeQY_6zRBqp_xZeDXTzU-3hinv2ED6pGhLTcftzyWAn_VbK2vmr8/4tb/YhiL3SgeS32phsXvz3f4XQ/h7/h001.0x86UMe4X7oftUqbrSh5BMTn30uu39b7Pq9zSMbwKN0)

Border SecurityCBP SEIZES $67 MILLION IN DRUGS AT SAN DIEGO PORTSWhat's Happening
* Customs and Border Protection's San Diego Field Office seized more than **$67 million** in illegal drugs across separate hauls in July, the Department of Homeland Security said in figures released this week.
* Officers intercepted **144 smuggling attempts** and seized 8,359 pounds of narcotics — including fentanyl, cocaine and methamphetamine — across seven ports of entry on the California–Mexico border.
* "Day after day, our officers remain steadfast in their mission to protect our communities and secure our borders," said San Diego Field Operations Director Sidney Aki.

The Situation
* DHS framed the seizures as part of the administration's broader crackdown to secure the southern border.
* The San Diego corridor has been a persistent smuggling route, including a recently uncovered cross-border tunnel between Tijuana and San Diego.
* A single month's haul at one field office underscores the scale of the fentanyl trade still pressing on the border.

The PerspectiveEvery pound of fentanyl stopped at the port is a life that might not be lost in a living room in Ohio or Arizona. Numbers like these are worth celebrating — they show what border officers can do when the mission is clear and they have the backing to carry it out. But a $67 million month at a single office is also a measure of how much poison is still trying to get through. The honest read is that enforcement is working and the fight is far from over. The answer is to keep resourcing the officers doing the work, not to pretend the problem is behind us.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_OnUGc7WMnXhOsv3ZZ0RLAuPIxrxMrLW215cdJO0en--cLb8UBkR17oriNY9SikwfbYuG4LowB-kxE2zz3rw_QSAUxsvsbwcrh6E9j_DIEnpbF4qMkOVyf3zIB3yFW6bjRQoHu1VnMz_-dvmY7ITBamw-iLgwW1vpiCXJo4r8u-lWmyv23TC9VNJDBcqOFcMXCDVgu4-xXiSPVFE9gbEtz_ZGJ0ex5IQsQ174b_nstrHhUoUB2GxnewvJ11hTHRUx5vRVXrpuqB88_EAzcMMEo85tAQ4Smj6dfvUReJX4hDRneRqVpAnya2BBF1__sHmqjKyNGR8KbydCjm4uEiDWFBP_prt7ssQ1S7SHRi-I3Wv/4tb/YhiL3SgeS32phsXvz3f4XQ/h8/h001.kag_ZbMogvsqMcseqhx0cuVG5RY8N8JqkfZQIzAhZLk)
| ⚡ The Bottom LineToday's news traces a single thread: leverage is only worth what it delivers. A ceasefire lapses because Tehran gambled that pressure would break before it did; tariffs bite at home as much as abroad; a toss-up in Alaska will turn on who convinces voters they can deliver; and a record drug haul shows enforcement paying off even as the threat persists. Strength and results are not the same thing — the country will judge this moment by the second, not the first. That's just the truth.

The United Arab Emirates said Iran fired two ballistic missiles toward the country Tuesday — one falling outside its territorial waters, the second inside them. Iran's foreign ministry denied launching them. A commercial vessel transiting the strait was struck by an "unknown projectile," killing one crew member, the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center reported. The Situation Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the strait will stay closed until Washington meets its commitments under the expired framework. President Trump has floated declaring the Strait of Hormuz U.S. territory and warned he would strike Oman if it interfered in negotiations. Brent crude climbed back above $90 a barrel , up roughly 2–3% over the prior 24 hours as traders priced in the risk to global oil flows. The PerspectiveA world that depends on the Strait of Hormuz cannot let Tehran treat it as a hostage. The administration is right to keep maximum pressure on a regime that walked away from the table rather than give up its leverage, and right to remind allies like Oman that neutrality cannot mean shielding an aggressor. Talk of annexing the strait is bluster that gets ahead of the facts on the ground, and the death of a merchant sailor is a sober reminder that the cost of this standoff is measured in lives, not just barrels. Peace is worth pursuing — but not a peace that hands Iran a veto over the world's energy lifeline. The EconomyNEW TARIFFS ON CANADIAN GOODS SET TO HIT THIS WEEKWhat's Happening A fresh round of U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports is set to take effect Wednesday after talks between Washington and Ottawa stalled. The duties would cover roughly $20 billion in goods, including some clothing, wines, dairy products, hockey sticks and building materials such as cement and plywood. Canadian broadcaster CBC reported the two sides were at an impasse despite weeks of meetings. The Situation Importers can pass the new duties on to shoppers, adding pressure on households already facing higher costs. Consumer prices are up about 3.4% over the past year, per NBC News — up from 2.4% before the Iran war began. Tariffs already cost the average American household roughly $1,100 a year, according to an estimate from Yale's Budget Lab. The PerspectiveTariffs are leverage, and used surgically they can pry open lopsided trade deals that Washington let fester for decades. But leverage has a price, and honesty requires admitting that some of that price lands on American families at the checkout counter. The right test is simple: are these duties delivering better terms and reshoring real production, or just adding a line item to the grocery bill? A deal with Canada that levels the field would vindicate the strategy. A stalemate that quietly raises prices while an election looms would not. Voters can tell the difference. The 2026 MapSULLIVAN AND PELTOLA ADVANCE IN ALASKA SENATE PRIMARYWhat's Happening Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK) and former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola advanced from Alaska's 16-candidate nonpartisan primary Tuesday. With about half the vote counted, Peltola led narrowly, 45.9% to Sullivan's 45% , according to the Associated Press. Under Alaska's system, the top four finishers advance to a ranked-choice general election in November. The Situation The Cook Political Report rates the seat a toss-up; Democrats need to net four seats to take the Senate. The Senate Leadership Fund has committed roughly $17 million to the race, adding $2 million this month to defend Sullivan. Trump carried Alaska by 13 points in 2024, and Peltola has kept her distance from national Democrats — her campaign declined a fundraising appeal from Kamala Harris's PAC. The PerspectiveAlaska is the kind of race that decides Senate majorities, and the early numbers should keep Republicans honest rather than complacent. Sullivan is a proven statewide winner in a state Trump carried comfortably, but Peltola has done it before, and her studied distance from Harris and the national party is a tell: even Democrats know their brand is a liability in flyover country. A primary is not a general election, and ranked-choice voting adds a wildcard that has burned the GOP here before. The lesson is to compete for every vote and let the contrast — commonsense versus a party lurching left — do the work. Border SecurityCBP SEIZES $67 MILLION IN DRUGS AT SAN DIEGO PORTSWhat's Happening Customs and Border Protection's San Diego Field Office seized more than $67 million in illegal drugs across separate hauls in July, the Department of Homeland Security said in figures released this week. Officers intercepted 144 smuggling attempts and seized 8,359 pounds of narcotics — including fentanyl, cocaine and methamphetamine — across seven ports of entry on the California–Mexico border. "Day after day, our officers remain steadfast in their mission to protect our communities and secure our borders," said San Diego Field Operations Director Sidney Aki. The Situation DHS framed the seizures as part of the administration's broader crackdown to secure the southern border. The San Diego corridor has been a persistent smuggling route, including a recently uncovered cross-border tunnel between Tijuana and San Diego. * A single month's haul at one field office underscores the scale of the fentanyl trade still pressing on the border. The PerspectiveEvery pound of fentanyl stopped at the port is a life that might not be lost in a living room in Ohio or Arizona. Numbers like these are worth celebrating — they show what border officers can do when the mission is clear and they have the backing to carry it out. But a $67 million month at a single office is also a measure of how much poison is still trying to get through. The honest read is that enforcement is working and the fight is far from over. The answer is to keep resourcing the officers doing the work, not to pretend the problem is behind us. | ⚡ The Bottom LineToday's news traces a single thread: leverage is only worth what it delivers. A ceasefire lapses because Tehran gambled that pressure would break before it did; tariffs bite at home as much as abroad; a toss-up in Alaska will turn on who convinces voters they can deliver; and a record drug haul shows enforcement paying off even as the threat persists. Wow, our interview with Hunter Biden lived up to everything we hoped and thought it could be. It turns out when Republicans went after Hunter Biden, they had no idea who they were messing with.
Hunter was equal parts thoughtful, gracious, forthcoming--on everything from his painting to Marjorie Taylor Greene's obsession with his junk--and most importantly, he was real. He avoided no questions, gave honest answers even when it would've been easier to move on, and shared inconvenient truths.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3893733f-0f73-420d-85c8-59fcf4605dd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
With all the hoopla put aside: we were talking to a son who loves his dad, suffered enormous family tragedy, as well as from drug addiction, and had to navigate a world where absolute ghouls used it to their political advantage. Yet he seems to have only come out stronger, at peace with his life, and also ready to take on Don Jr. in a UFC ring anytime Don's is clear-eyed (and brained) enough to do it. So likely never.
Republicans made Hunter famous. They didn't count on how talented, intelligent, and charismatic he is. And they'll be paying the price for that for a long time. Watch the video for all the details on his father's health, Hunter's recovery, his art, a forthcoming book, his disdain for human chucklehead/corporate-media, street-walker, Jake Tapper, and the feeling you'll get that from him, the best is still yet to come.

name: Ted Cruz
subject: I sat alone in that room and thought of my father
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
A witness read from a 1991 document that should terrify every American. And I thought of my father. Democrats boycotted my hearing.

| | | | [](https://trk.email.tedcruz.-h8OD7zrRXzhwDOgA6WSA)
---
| | | Fellow Conservative, This week I chaired a Senate hearing on Muslim Brotherhood influence operations in America. Every Senate Democrat boycotted. They released a statement calling my hearing a _"political creepshow."_ They said that confronting this threat was Islamophobia. They walked out before a single witness testified. _I held the hearing anyway._ And sitting alone at that dais -- I thought about my father. He fled Cuba with nothing but the shirt on his back. He had been tortured in a Cuban prison. He watched his country -- a beautiful, thriving country -- get destroyed by people who also called their critics fear-mongers and political theatrics. People who infiltrated the universities first, then the media, then the institutions, then the government -- until there was nothing left to infiltrate because they owned all of it. **In 1991, the Muslim Brotherhood wrote an internal memorandum outlining their strategy for the United States. A witness read from it under oath in my hearing room this week.** Their stated goal: infiltrate American universities, media outlets, and research centers. _That was their plan in 1991. The witnesses testified that this is exactly what has happened._ The White House's own 2026 counter-terrorism strategy calls the Muslim Brotherhood "the root of all modern Islamist terrorism." The United States has already designated Brotherhood branches as terrorist organizations. Egypt. Saudi Arabia. The UAE. All designated them. And Senate Democrats won't sit in a room and talk about it. They want to ignore the facts. They walk out. They cover their ears and hope you aren't paying attention. **_I have seen this before. My father lived it._** The playbook is always the same. Infiltrate the institutions. Silence the critics. Call anyone who speaks up a bigot or a political opportunist. And by the time enough people realize what's happening -- it's too late. My father lost his country that way. Slowly, then all at once.**I refuse to lose ours.** That is why I am still fighting. In that hearing room alone. On the Senate floor. In this race. Every single day. But before I finalize our strategy for the final push to November -- I need to know where you stand. I need to know if conservatives across this country see what I'm seeing and are ready to fight back. **Please take my Official 2026 Midterm Conservative Survey right now. It will take two minutes.** **[[LINK]](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)** **_The left is organized. They are funded. They have a plan that dates back to 1991. And they are counting on you to stay quiet._****Please don't.** **[[BEGIN 2026 MIDTERM SURVEY->]](https://trk.email.tedcruz.-yVsD5Q-3gjbzCOGw)** My father lost his country once. **I refuse to lose ours.** For liberty, Ted Cruz _
_U.S. Senator - Texas

body:
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13369?t=1001&akid=1816%2E181023%2ELhbCLz ][IMG]

Hi there,

It’s Winnie Brinks. I am humbled to officially announce that I am running
alongside Jocelyn Benson to be your next Lieutenant Governor.

There’s a lot of work to do from now until Election Day, and everyone here
on Team Benson-Brinks for Michigan is running full steam ahead to win big
in November and make Michigan a place where everyone can stay and thrive.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13369?t=1002&akid=1816%2E181023%2ELhbCLz ]I’ll tell you a little bit more about myself in a moment, but first I
have to ask: will you make a donation to our campaign today and help us
kick off the next stage of this race on the best foot possible?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13369?t=1003&akid=1816%2E181023%2ELhbCLz ]DONATE →

I have to be honest: Growing up, I never
would’ve imagined I’d run for office, let alone be running to be your next
Lieutenant Governor.

I grew up on my family’s dairy farm, the daughter of two Dutch immigrants.
My first job was feeding the calves and putting up the hay. My paycheck
came in the form of a steer I could raise and sell for a profit.

My background isn’t typical of most folks representing us in Lansing, but
I think that’s a good thing.

My background taught me the importance of hard work, resilience, and
service to others. They’re lessons I’ve carried throughout my life, from
working in education to serving my community as a non-profit caseworker,
and they’re lessons I instilled in my three daughters.

Even my first run for office was anything but typical. I ran a write-in
campaign to even get on the ballot because my neighbors needed a voice
fighting for them, not corporations and mega-donors.

Over the years, I’ve spent countless hours knocking on the doors of my
neighbors because I fundamentally believe: good government should be about
people.

As both a State Representative and State Senator — where I became the
first woman to serve as Michigan's Senate Majority Leader — I've been
proud to fight to ensure every Michigander has a voice, from investing in
public education to protecting healthcare to cutting costs and making life
more affordable for Michiganders.

I’m ready to continue the fight alongside Jocelyn Benson because we still
have a lot of work to do to protect Michigan families.

This race isn’t going to be easy. It’s shaping up to be one of the most
competitive gubernatorial races in the country.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13369?t=1004&akid=1816%2E181023%2ELhbCLz ]We need all hands on deck to make sure we hit the ground running in
this next stage of the campaign, so can we count on you to rush a donation
today and help us win in November?

20 issues, 20 days. Day 1/20

| |

| | _With just twenty days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 20, I am highlighting the relationship between Israel and Palestine, and the need for an open, honest, and compassionate conversation about the issue here in the United States._
* * *
Dear David, Israel and Palestine. I know the grief, anguish, and anger that this subject evokes in so many people with a deep and abiding commitment to their faith, to human rights, to ancestral homelands, to peace, and to the wellbeing of children. As a scholar of religion, history, and policy, I have grappled with this in my classes and on the campaign trail. I know that not everyone who reads this email will agree when I call what Israel is doing to the Palestinian people a genocide. I know that many people who read this email have different visions for what peace and justice and the future look like for Israeli and Palestinian people. And, we need a Democratic Party that can have that conversation. This is why I was paying close attention when earlier this week, the _New Hampshire Union Leader_ published an accounting of the donations to candidates in this race linked with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC). [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/vrSzyRjRq6CoYT7oJF2F1g~~/AAUS1hA~/FWo5XDU4SvpJPHKcDAufX_As1fbPYogMATvTL0C61BMtyrGcZcNImddLdMNlQsZJJ3FZtu6XOZd9knjuXiZ71mjbKqxICnsCxVkM1rR0B34tpvSqyF4SvfMVHdMyAadEvFi7xJ2tWK1UFTFGhjpUu_ynWxV4AVEaejnuUQa9EsC12tpxo5j_PrH14qkDqWjucVkTRfhZ6tzk4rt1__LIYXwaFZW9hqpdwEdG0sSC7OgxANaP7gNohetoQRSi7xy6p7-MQycRsuptyvEaAMq0Rw~~) The report showed that our campaign received one donation from a person who also contributed to AIPAC. We checked in with the reporter and followed up. They were correct. So I refunded the contribution. Not because I think that a single $500 contribution from someone who also supports AIPAC will influence the way I would approach this issue in Congress, but because **AIPAC has spent hundreds of millions of dollars on elections this cycle in an attempt to ensure that we _cannot_ have an open and honest conversation about what is happening in Israel and Palestine.** The same is true of AI and Crypto PACs spreading false and deceptive messages and backing candidates who will allow these companies to write the legislation that will determine the role their technology plays in our lives for decades. **This is why I am calling on all candidates in this primary to refund contributions from individuals linked to AIPAC, Crypto, and AI special interests** that are attempting to manipulate Democratic primaries and elect candidates who are willing to compromise on core democratic values in an attempt to gain power over our political and economic system. And, that’s why we’ve relied on nurses, small-business owners, teachers, first responders, mechanics, and people like you to help us build this campaign from the ground up. **[Because when I go to Washington, it will be to continue a conversation with YOU. **Mayor Zohran Mamdani just recorded the lowest level of violent crime in New York City’s history.**

He’s brought down crime by taking 1,000 guns off NYC streets. He’s implemented youth safety zones, making sure kids are safe on their way to school and in classrooms. And, he’s addressing the root causes of crime – expanding access to jobs and lowering the cost of housing.

# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=722%2E127862%2EOl4DTk)
Folks, I'm going to be frank with you.
MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo, Donald Trump, and the billionaires bankrolling this race think they can buy their way to victory this November.

Friend, A recent report from the U.S. Government Accountability Office found that millions of workers — including thousands at Amazon — still need Medicaid and SNAP just to get by as Amazon's profits soared into the tens of billions. Another report dug into DOGE's "Wall of Receipts," Elon Musk's much-hyped tally of government savings. Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** An audit found that Riverdale Peaks II Metro District levies 115 mills [yet can't fully pay its bonds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) — one of 19 districts the audit flagged for debt trouble. Another audit flagged 13 school districts, including Cherry Creek and Poudre, for [shrinking reserves](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), though districts call it planned. Colorado's ballot initiative process increasingly [favors deep-pocketed interests](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And Douglas County launched an initiative to [cut permitting red tape](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Lake Mead and Lake Powell [hit record-low water levels](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), putting Hoover Dam's hydropower at risk. The Milwaukee Election Commission is reviewing the ["human error" that delayed 28,000 absentee ballots ](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)last week.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Scott Bessent [credited mass deportations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) with rising wages and falling rents, though a Townhall piece said that's only part of the affordability fix. Deroy Murdock criticized Cornyn and Tillis for [killing Trump's $1.776 billion "Justice Fund,"](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) noting the Judgment Fund remains available. A New York Post editorial warned [women now outnumber men in the workforce](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for only the third time in history. And Cory Gaines argued AG Phil Weiser's office [withholds lawsuit details from its tracker](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, August 19, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[This metro district charges 115 mills and is still behind on its bonds. A state audit found it isn’t alone.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Homeowners inside the Riverdale Peaks II Metropolitan District pay one of the highest tax rates of any special district in Colorado. Their metro district levied 115.019 mills in 2024, good for fifth place on a list of eleven districts statewide charging 100 mills or more. That levy pulled in $428,566 in property taxes for the year.
Riverdale Peaks II is one of 19 districts that told the state, in their own financial filings, that they have been or will be unable to make principal or interest payments on their debt as those payments come due.
It taxes its residents at more than 100 mills and still reports to the state that it can’t keep up with the full payments on its bonds. That combination is the core finding of a state audit released in June, one a search of Colorado news coverage turns up no reporting on.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Cherry Creek, Poudre among Colorado districts flagged for draining reserves](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_State auditors flag three of Colorado's largest, most visible school districts for burning through reserves — even as districts insist the drawdowns were deliberate, not distress._
* **Big districts join a growing list:** Cherry Creek, Colorado Springs 11, and Poudre — three of Colorado's largest districts, enrolling a combined 108,000+ students — were newly flagged by the State Auditor for missing two or more fiscal-health benchmarks, joining a list that grew to 13 districts as the total missing at least one benchmark climbed to 43, up from 35 the year before.
* **Districts insist it was planned spending, not shortfalls:** Cherry Creek's fund balance fell from $99.5 million to $71.2 million to boost employee compensation; Colorado Springs 11 drew its reserves down from a $126.1 million peak to $93.9 million under a board-approved strategy; and Poudre cited legal settlements, staff bonuses, and pandemic-era reserve buildup for its $12.9 million drop.
* **A wider funding squeeze looms:** Even as the state's Budget Stabilization Factor hit zero and property tax revenue jumped $421.7 million statewide, 29 districts serving roughly 52,000 students remain "held harmless" at 2024-25 funding levels — absorbing rising costs with no formula increase for two years running.

Peter, did you see this?
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137547747/641140599/-2016015222?refcode=em26_260819_RFKjr_fnd_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260819_RFKjr_fnd_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=9f4467b4-119c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZjQ0NjdiNC0xMTljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FV82ttfO32YgkuPqHnGqFNA4ppM73Jz1LuNNfxHmOZs=)
On Monday, Mariannette Miller-Meeks brought in a special guest to tout her efforts to improve the health of Iowa's youth: RFK Jr...

They announced the return of the _Presidential Fitness Test_ to Iowa public schools, and spewed lies and attacks about our education system.

All while forgetting to mention that **Miller-Meeks voted to cut Medicaid and Medicare for thousands of families in Iowa.** She also proudly voted to **cut the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) by nearly $300 million — literally taking food out of the mouths of hungry children.**

Peter, physical activity is great, especially for children as they develop (in school, Christina did cheerleading, track, and baton twirling!). But push-ups and burpees do _nothing_ when kids don't have access to healthcare or the nutrition they need to grow. Every stop was a conversation about what it means to have a congressman who actually shows up.

| | | | |

Hey Peter,
_72 hours. 17 counties. All of TN-05._
That was the commitment Chaz made after winning the primary, and he made good on it. From Memphis along the Mississippi River to Tiptonville and Union City in the northwest, through Paris and Clarksville, down through the rural heart of West Tennessee, and back home to Columbia where this campaign started
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/YljlCyGydLjFON9ndU35HA~~/AAUS1hA~/kAHEKUvmAl-1eJkpd54QaOY1TKDrsRIoCGF0kbvchS2vXJqnUZCNKmjV_fcC4vg8pQB5rRDvNK51HlCU6SKIQNlfsBbahMpwTHBeltRMDUllVOiHPlm2qt-bAXudWdSuYJcO-weZrGPtG5DM1tJdyhQLCUJyR6rto5zLJJKkmMO2fun9YmKqxQHe50hytDpLGRq3yAV9fg-i8km-ZYEzCLnbCvmUIGFP3nY1vLstmsewNtTfM5MxhOspM22FRfgf)
Every stop was a conversation. About gas prices and grocery bills. About farmers getting squeezed and families stretched thin. About what it actually means to have a congressman who shows up, not just at election time, but every single day.
Chaz ended the tour the way he started this campaign, right at home in Columbia, at the same church he grew up in, with Liz and the kids beside him.
This is what the next few months are going to look like. All 17 counties. Every corner of this district. No shortcuts.

clean_body: Every stop was a conversation about what it means to have a congressman who actually shows up. | | | | | Hey Peter, 72 hours. 17 counties. All of TN-05. That was the commitment Chaz made after winning the primary, and he made good on it. From Memphis along the Mississippi River to Tiptonville and Union City in the northwest, through Paris and Clarksville, down through the rural heart of West Tennessee, and back home to Columbia where this campaign started Every stop was a conversation. About gas prices and grocery bills. About farmers getting squeezed and families stretched thin. About what it actually means to have a congressman who shows up, not just at election time, but every single day. Chaz ended the tour the way he started this campaign, right at home in Columbia, at the same church he grew up in, with Liz and the kids beside him. This is what the next few months are going to look like. All 17 counties. Every corner of this district. No shortcuts. | | The future of Texas is in good hands. **One of the brightest joys of my summer has been getting to know and work with the young leaders who will carry the torch of democratic leadership into tomorrow.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548105/641141597/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) My team and I had the privilege of welcoming eleven outstanding young leaders to the 2026 Frontera Fellows program. Throughout this summer, these dynamic young leaders learned the ins and outs of campaign strategy, legislative strategy, community organizing, and most importantly, what it means to move beyond the confines of policy and political strategy to deeply understand the community we represent. Our fellows had the opportunity to meet with leaders driving change right here in Texas 16, like School District Trustee Manny Rodriguez and El Paso ISD Trustee Mindy Sutton. They also met with titans in the Democratic Party, like James Talarico, Representative Mary González, and many other great community leaders. For the final chapter of this year's program, our fellows drew on their unique experiences and perspectives to build projects that tackle a variety of community challenges, ranging from accessibility and transportation to civic engagement and youth literacy, as well as much-needed support for migrants and refugees that centers care and humanity. Please join me in celebrating our Fellows by reading and uplifting these phenomenal four final projects, which stand as a testament to their dedication and summer-long learning: [**Annunciation House Community Drive is **](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548106/641141599/-903390740?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883)**[led](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548107/641141600/-903390740?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) **by Paulina Ortega and Daniela Avant-Mier. This project aims to support the organizations in El Paso that work directly with our migrant and immigrant communities. By placing collection boxes throughout El Paso, Paulina and Daniela hope to show their profound appreciation and support for organizations like the Annunciation House, Estrella del Paso, and Las Americas Immigrant Advocacy Center, which dedicate their time to helping others. Members of the community can support their project by donating, volunteering, and learning more about the organizations that show up for some of our most vulnerable communities. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548109/641141601/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) **[The Public Transportation Resource Guide](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548111/641141603/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883)** is led by Kareena Ortiz, Pierro Aragones, and Santiago Serrano. Their project focuses on identifying accessibility gaps in El Paso's public transportation system and developing recommendations to bridge them for underserved communities. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548114/641141605/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) [**The Youth Civic Engagement Initiative**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548116/641141608/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) is a civic engagement project led by Randall Barraza, Alina Varela, Sandra Lozano, and Nathaly Riojas that revolves around the development of an Instagram page geared towards highlighting local government and civic news in an accessible manner for young people in the community. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548118/641141610/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) [**The 915 Reads**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548120/641141612/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) is a community book drive initiative led by Sophia Espinosa, YuHee Kim, and Emma Lopez to benefit local women's and children's organizations. Their project aims to address and highlight declining literacy rates by collecting as many books as possible so they can be given to local children within the community. **I am beyond proud of all that the Frontera Fellows have learned and accomplished in such a short time. We've spent the past several weeks cultivating their skills, helping them find their voices, and asking them how they can make a difference in their communities.** Please uplift their accomplishments and celebrate their dedication by reading the full article, written by Frontera Fellow Emma Lopez, about their summer of learning and each of their final projects. [Read The Article](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137548122/641141614/-2086290552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5Nzg0YzgwOC0xMzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ttsLj1A5eGzhFEuOlW8QEXZOjMoBFnttK2rSWJtSV8Q=&emci=5800f3bf-fa9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9784c808-139c-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14565883) When we meaningfully invest in the leaders of tomorrow, everyone wins. I truly believe that — and I cannot wait to see what the future holds for the 2026 Frontera Fellows cohort! clean_body: | | | | The future of Texas is in good hands. One of the brightest joys of my summer has been getting to know and work with the young leaders who will carry the torch of democratic leadership into tomorrow. My team and I had the privilege of welcoming eleven outstanding young leaders to the 2026 Frontera Fellows program. Throughout this summer, these dynamic young leaders learned the ins and outs of campaign strategy, legislative strategy, community organizing, and most importantly, what it means to move beyond the confines of policy and political strategy to deeply understand the community we represent. Our fellows had the opportunity to meet with leaders driving change right here in Texas 16, like School District Trustee Manny Rodriguez and El Paso ISD Trustee Mindy Sutton. They also met with titans in the Democratic Party, like James Talarico, Representative Mary González, and many other great community leaders. For the final chapter of this year's program, our fellows drew on their unique experiences and perspectives to build projects that tackle a variety of community challenges, ranging from accessibility and transportation to civic engagement and youth literacy, as well as much-needed support for migrants and refugees that centers care and humanity. Please join me in celebrating our Fellows by reading and uplifting these phenomenal four final projects, which stand as a testament to their dedication and summer-long learning: by Paulina Ortega and Daniela Avant-Mier. This project aims to support the organizations in El Paso that work directly with our migrant and immigrant communities. By placing collection boxes throughout El Paso, Paulina and Daniela hope to show their profound appreciation and support for organizations like the Annunciation House, Estrella del Paso, and Las Americas Immigrant Advocacy Center, which dedicate their time to helping others. Members of the community can support their project by donating, volunteering, and learning more about the organizations that show up for some of our most vulnerable communities. is led by Kareena Ortiz, Pierro Aragones, and Santiago Serrano. Their project focuses on identifying accessibility gaps in El Paso's public transportation system and developing recommendations to bridge them for underserved communities. is a civic engagement project led by Randall Barraza, Alina Varela, Sandra Lozano, and Nathaly Riojas that revolves around the development of an Instagram page geared towards highlighting local government and civic news in an accessible manner for young people in the community. is a community book drive initiative led by Sophia Espinosa, YuHee Kim, and Emma Lopez to benefit local women's and children's organizations. Their project aims to address and highlight declining literacy rates by collecting as many books as possible so they can be given to local children within the community. I am beyond proud of all that the Frontera Fellows have learned and accomplished in such a short time. We've spent the past several weeks cultivating their skills, helping them find their voices, and asking them how they can make a difference in their communities. Please uplift their accomplishments and celebrate their dedication by reading the full article, written by Frontera Fellow Emma Lopez, about their summer of learning and each of their final projects. When we meaningfully invest in the leaders of tomorrow, everyone wins. I truly believe that — and I cannot wait to see what the future holds for the 2026 Frontera Fellows cohort!
