Chip in $25 today and help us unseat Tom Cotton." | | ---|---|--- In the video, Shoffner ranted and raved about Cotton's calls for accountability for the Biden administration's failed COVID policies, saying: " But it's not helpful for Tom Cotton to whine and complain about what someone did five years ago." Shoffner's March statement sounds awfully similar to the Senate Democrats' attitude this week regarding Dr. Fauci's testimony, as not one Senate Democrat cared to criticize Fauci after he took the Fifth Amendment over questions related to Biden's failed COVID-era policies. It is also worth noting that, as Dr. Fauci walked into the United States Senate hearing, Loomer Unleashed asked him to apologize for his past criticisms of President Trump. After Fauci refused, we called him an embarrassment to his face. We witnessed firsthand Fauci and the Senate Democrats' lack of remorse for their failed COVID policies. It was quite a remarkable sight to see that shocked the entire nation. Shoffner has donated to current Senate Democrats who supported the numerous failed COVID policies of the Biden administration, which Fauci's lockdowns helped create. FEC records show Shoffner previously donated to Senator Elizabeth Warren, who signed a 2021 letter addressed to the Biden administration in which she asked Biden to open up the strategic oil reserves--the original issue Cotton was attacking the Biden administration over. | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Remember, the strategic reserves had to be opened because when Biden came into office, he essentially allowed Fauci to lock down the country and implement vaccine and mask mandates, harming America's energy production. Add in the fact that Shoffner is also a Kamala Harris donor, and Kamala Harris was Vice President when Biden released the strategic reserves in 2021, and it becomes clear where Shoffner stands on the Biden administration's failed COVID policies, and the depletion of America's strategic oil reserves. | | ---|---|--- Shoffner has also been awfully quiet about what she thinks of Dr. Fauci himself. However, she has a history of donating to Fauci fan girls Kamala Harris and Elizabeth Warren, with Kamala once posting to her X account in 2020: " We'll listen to Dr. Fauci. And we'll listen to the science. That's how we will get through this--together." | | ---|---|--- Elizabeth Warren once demanded Americans listen to Fauci, posting: " Listen to the scientists. Listen to the public health experts. Listen to the facts and data. Listen to the doctors and nurses and emergency responders on the front lines. Listen to Dr. Fauci." | | ---|---|--- As we have exposed, Shoffner has embraced Elizabeth Warren and Kamala Harris's anti-ICE and pro-Green New Deal policies, so it is reasonable to believe Shoffner is also a closeted Fauci fan girl like Harris and Warren, whom she has financially supported. Either way, Shoffner telling voters to get over themselves when it comes to securing accountability for the Biden administration's failed COVID policies is yet another example of why Arkansas voters must ensure Tom Cotton wins reelection by record margins in November. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

**Justin’s neighborhood in South Memphis is sandwiched between two of the city’s biggest polluters. And both are owned by Elon Musk, the richest man in the world.**

clean_body: Help Justin Pearson fight back. | You’re hearing a lot about data centers these days, and for good reason. These energy-guzzlers often begin building with zero local input, while families and local businesses are left to foot the bill of skyrocketing energy costs and even more toxic pollution. It’s quickly becoming one of the defining climate fights of our time. And one of the leaders at the center of that fight is JanePAC climate champion, Justin Pearson: = Justin Pearson is bravely taking the fight for climate justice to Congress.And whoever wins this race for Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District could help define federal policy on data centers. = | = Justin Pearson is no stranger to powerful corporations treating Memphis like a sacrifice zone. Before he was an elected official, Justin led a grassroots movement that successfully stopped the multibillion-dollar crude oil Byhalia Pipeline from cutting through Memphis’s predominantly Black and low-income neighborhoods. Now, he’s fighting another massive corporate polluter in his own backyard: Elon Musk’s xAI. Justin’s neighborhood in South Memphis is sandwiched between two of the city’s biggest polluters. And both are owned by Elon Musk, the richest man in the world. According to multiple environmental groups who are now suing Musk’s xAI, these methane gas turbines could emit more than 2,500 tons of smog-forming pollution every single year. That poisoned air is getting pumped into an area where the rates of emergency room visits for asthma are already the highest in the state. We simply can’t afford a world where Justin isn't representing TN-09 in Congress. He’s the fighter demanding better for Memphis, while polluters like Elon Musk see this community as little more than an opportunity to line their pockets. **= = ✊ In solidarity, Team JanePAC | Follow along: | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. Hey Peter,
---
Last week was super busy, with several meet-and-greets, a public TV interview, a canvass, and speaking at the Voters of Tomorrow conference. These activities gave me the chance to speak with voters in our district and keep a promise that matters a ton to me: _**showing**_** _ up for our community._** I have our wonderful community to thank for reminding me exactly what we are working for. At the Voters of Tomorrow event, I was so glad to see the next generation energized to drive political change and use their voices. I was also reminded of how important it is that the work we do now sets up the next generation for success. Growing up, I was active in my local Boy Scout troop. We took lots of hikes, and the rule always was both “leave no trace” AND “leave things a bit better than we found them.” The same principle should apply to those in public service. Leaders should always seek to hand things off to the next generation in better shape than they found it. It’s hard to argue that’s happening today. That’s why we need a new generation of elected representatives. And like I told the folks at the Voters of Tomorrow event, we’ve got an opportunity this November to send a new group of leaders to Washington, DC, who can do just that. The goal is a better, stronger government, and I hope to work together with fellow leaders in Washington to make that a reality. Each interaction we have with voters and members in the district underscores that we’re on the right track: working to address the wrongs Washington is currently serving up. clean_body: The same principles apply to government| | | | = Hey Peter, Last week was super busy, with several meet-and-greets, a public TV interview, a canvass, and speaking at the Voters of Tomorrow conference. These activities gave me the chance to speak with voters in our district and keep a promise that matters a ton to me: showing up for our community. I have our wonderful community to thank for reminding me exactly what we are working for. At the Voters of Tomorrow event, I was so glad to see the next generation energized to drive political change and use their voices. I was also reminded of how important it is that the work we do now sets up the next generation for success. Growing up, I was active in my local Boy Scout troop. We took lots of hikes, and the rule always was both “leave no trace” AND “leave things a bit better than we found them.” The same principle should apply to those in public service. Leaders should always seek to hand things off to the next generation in better shape than they found it. It’s hard to argue that’s happening today. That’s why we need a new generation of elected representatives. And like I told the folks at the Voters of Tomorrow event, we’ve got an opportunity this November to send a new group of leaders to Washington, DC, who can do just that. The goal is a better, stronger government, and I hope to work together with fellow leaders in Washington to make that a reality. Each interaction we have with voters and members in the district underscores that we’re on the right track: working to address the wrongs Washington is currently serving up. more meet-and-greets, town halls, and outreach events we can host, the more people who know about this race. = Every conversation I’ve had over this campaign has given me so much more insight into the changes we need in Washington. We cannot keep settling for the corrupt mess we have been handed. Talk more soon, Paul Barringer Candidate for US Congress P.S. | | Friend,

The Republican primary is over, and my opponent this November is Jay Schroeder.

He calls himself an "**authentic MAGA activist** ," and he is running for Secretary of State on a promise to eliminate the bipartisan commission that oversees our elections and pull that power into this office himself. In 2022, he told a Republican crowd that he would not have signed the certification of the 2020 presidential election here in Wisconsin.

| Tom Tiffany already tried to overturn an election once. Tiffany voted against certifying the 2020 results, he joined a lawsuit to throw out Wisconsin's own presidential votes, and he said he would have objected to Wisconsin's electoral votes on the floor if he had been given the chance. He is Donald Trump's hand-picked candidate and votes with Trump 100% of the time.

Put them together and the danger is obvious. **Two men who tried to throw out your vote, running the two offices that help certify it.**

I am running to stop that. I want to do this job honestly, protect the integrity of our results, and steward the trust funds that help fund school libraries from Kenosha to Superior. With David Crowley in the governor's office and me as your Secretary of State, no one will throw out your vote.

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/hItRzgpn69u?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

name: Kerry McQuisten (Newsletter)
subject: Wedding Vows & a Book Release!
body:
| | | | |
# We did it!
---
---
The biggest news! Solomon and I have officially tied the knot! Instead of renting a venue, we decided to bring the place in Polk County up to a wedding-worthy sparkle - then ended up doing much of the work ourselves. Completely worth it. We had a house filled with friends and family we love from around the globe, the United States, and Oregon. Some running for office. Some from conservative organizations or the media. Some from inside the Trump administration. Others from completely outside the world of politics. Beautiful flowers, good food, the best photographer we could ask for, a framed congratulatory letter from POTUS on the wall, and vows during which people laughed out loud and maybe shed a tear or two. Vance Day, whose boss is new U.S. AG Todd Blanche, missed the Trump-attended swearing-in thanks to being here to officiate - and we're thankful he did! Hopefully, we hit that sweet spot between elegant and comfortable so that our guests actually enjoyed themselves. The only hitch was a weather problem in Florida and unrelated mechanical issues for some connecting in Chicago, which kept a few of our guests from getting here from back east. It seems that every wedding has guests who RSVP and then silently no-show as well, so in the end, the local church that loaned us their shuttle van ended up with those donated meals, which worked out well.
Right now, we're catching up with work demands within our companies. (I just signed an amazing new author.) August is kind of a political pause for us before we hit the airports again in September to tackle what we hope is the final stretch toward ending double taxation of overseas Americans. We definitely needed the break, and I can tell you with all sincerity that married life is fantastic and we're very happy.

---
# The Book is Out!
---
---
On July 4 to celebrate America's 250th birthday, Solomon and I released his new book, COUNTERSCRIPT.
“... riveting, heartwarming, and most of all—inspiring. America is strong because it welcomes those who know the enduring value of freedom.”
—Gordon G. Chang, Political Analyst

“... a blend of two great missions—love of all that makes America great and a warrior’s charge to defeat the evil he escaped.”
—Steve Yates, White House Deputy National Security Advisor (2001-2005)

“Solomon is a good friend of mine and of _freedom_. What he writes is important and true. Please read this and _hear _it.”
—Tommy Hicks, Former RNC Co-Chair; National Finance Co-Chair of Donald J. Trump for President, Inc.

"Gripping, deeply personal ... this book is impossible to ignore and difficult to put down.”
—Jennifer Van Laar, Managing Editor of RedState

There are two full pages of these reviews inside the book! You can buy a copy here, but keep in mind that the hardcover on Amazon is a case laminate hardcover. clean_body: | | | | | We did it! The biggest news! Solomon and I have officially tied the knot! Instead of renting a venue, we decided to bring the place in Polk County up to a wedding-worthy sparkle - then ended up doing much of the work ourselves. Completely worth it. We had a house filled with friends and family we love from around the globe, the United States, and Oregon. Some running for office. Some from conservative organizations or the media. Some from inside the Trump administration. Others from completely outside the world of politics. Beautiful flowers, good food, the best photographer we could ask for, a framed congratulatory letter from POTUS on the wall, and vows during which people laughed out loud and maybe shed a tear or two. Vance Day, whose boss is new U.S. AG Todd Blanche, missed the Trump-attended swearing-in thanks to being here to officiate - and we're thankful he did! Hopefully, we hit that sweet spot between elegant and comfortable so that our guests actually enjoyed themselves. The only hitch was a weather problem in Florida and unrelated mechanical issues for some connecting in Chicago, which kept a few of our guests from getting here from back east. It seems that every wedding has guests who RSVP and then silently no-show as well, so in the end, the local church that loaned us their shuttle van ended up with those donated meals, which worked out well. Right now, we're catching up with work demands within our companies. (I just signed an amazing new author.) August is kind of a political pause for us before we hit the airports again in September to tackle what we hope is the final stretch toward ending double taxation of overseas Americans. We definitely needed the break, and I can tell you with all sincerity that married life is fantastic and we're very happy. The Book is Out! On July 4 to celebrate America's 250th birthday, Solomon and I released his new book, COUNTERSCRIPT. “... riveting, heartwarming, and most of all—inspiring. America is strong because it welcomes those who know the enduring value of freedom.” —Gordon G. Chang, Political Analyst “... a blend of two great missions—love of all that makes America great and a warrior’s charge to defeat the evil he escaped.” —Steve Yates, White House Deputy National Security Advisor (2001-2005) “Solomon is a good friend of mine and of freedom. What he writes is important and true. Please read this and hear it.” —Tommy Hicks, Former RNC Co-Chair; National Finance Co-Chair of Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. "Gripping, deeply personal ... this book is impossible to ignore and difficult to put down.” —Jennifer Van Laar, Managing Editor of RedState There are two full pages of these reviews inside the book! You can buy a copy here, but keep in mind that the hardcover on Amazon is a case laminate hardcover. The hardcover everywhere else is a jacketed hardcover, which is much nicer! COUNTERSCRIPT is available in Kindle and paperback, and audio is coming within the next couple weeks. Links: ~~ ~ OCC's Trump Day Dinner | | | | | | The held our annual dinner and awards ceremony at the end of June to celebrate our hard-working members and hear some behind-the-scenes stories from keynote speaker Jennifer Van Laar, managing editor of RedState. Candidate for state rep in HD32, Max Sherman, also spoke to our group. Oregon voters - this is one of the seats with the potential of being flipped. We'd also all really like to see Cyrus Javadi out, right?! We don't want a Dem supermajority that can shove through any new tax they want, right?! Getting elected takes money. I'm not affiliated with Max's campaign, but I'm sure any amount helps. name: Sherrod Brown
subject: I won't start now
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY HICKENLOOPER FOR COLORADO
body:
Hi there, Today, I’m asking you to split $10 between my campaign and John Hickenlooper. The reason being: I don’t spend my time asking corporate bigwigs for massive checks. I don’t rely on billionaires to swoop in and save me when I’m in trouble. body:
Hegseth did not adequately prepare the military for this war, and the men and women fighting it are paying the price.
#
Peter, one of the main questions that must be asked about the deprivations the Lincoln Carrier Strike Group has been put through is simple:
Why?
Why are they running out of food? Why are they running out of the basics, like deodorant and toothpaste? Why did things get so bad that they couldn’t run maintenance and upkeep on those ships? Why have they gone more than 200 days without a port call?
Turns out, the answer is simple. It’s because Pete Hegseth is a liar, and a fool.
In the first days of the war, Iran inflicted significant damage on a Navy logistics hub in Bahrain. The Navy was forced to reorient their supply chains to a British base, Diego Garcia — which is 2200 miles from the Gulf of Oman, where the Lincoln Strike Group is deployed.
This happened because Hegseth jumped into this war with no plan. Hegseth did not adequately prepare the military for this war, and the men and women fighting it are paying the price.
But the problem is more than Hegseth’s incompetence, significant as it may be. Hegseth covered up the fact that the base in Bahrain was destroyed, alongside many other bases and facilities in the region. He hid the problem. And when you hide a problem as serious as this, things only get worse.
And ultimately, the root of this problem is crystal clear. Republican Senators greenlit Pete Hegseth’s nomination as Secretary of Defense. They were warned. They knew then that they were confirming the least prepared, least qualified SecDef in history. They did it anyway.
If that isn’t reason enough to raise hell and make sure Democrats retake the Senate this year, we don’t know what else might convince you.

name: Nellie Pou
subject: My priorities
body:
Here's what I'm fighting for

| |
---
Friend, People ask me all the time what I'm actually trying to get done in Washington. So, I wanted to share a few of my priorities: **Affordability.** I'm fighting to bring down housing and health care costs, and to make sure working families aren't the ones absorbing the cost of bad decisions made in Washington. **Accountability.** When I see federal agencies mismanaging funds or immigration enforcement operating without oversight, I don't look away. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: The truth about health care
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260819-6615-footer&t=1001&akid=6615%2E420207%2E0f09Ql ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

Americans are sick and tired of leaders who refuse to fight for them.

Sick and tired of being told to wait, to settle, and to accept a cruel,
for-profit healthcare system that puts corporate profits ahead of their
lives.

Sick and tired of watching politicians take Big Pharma’s money, protect
the status quo, and then throw up their hands and claim there’s nothing
they can do.

I hear it everywhere I go.

The demand is clear: bold, unapologetic leadership that will fight to make
our lives more affordable.

And at the top of that list, every single time? Healthcare.

Peter, I’ve spent
my career fighting to make healthcare a right — not a privilege reserved
for those who can afford it.

Nearly a decade ago, I introduced the Medicare for All Act because I knew
we could build a healthcare system that puts people, not profits, first.
I’ve proudly reintroduced it in every session since.

And I’m not backing down now.

After everything I’ve seen this summer — the grassroots organizing, the
growing progressive movement, and the strong, inspiring candidates proudly
running on Medicare for All — I know this fight is stronger than ever.

We have the people. We have the movement. And we have what it takes to win
Medicare for All. Now we need to keep organizing, keep fighting, and make
sure every working family in America can finally get the healthcare they
deserve.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260819.gwYTWB&refcode=em20260819-6615&amount=3&t=1002&akid=6615%2E420207%2E0f09Ql ]If you’re with me, will you pitch in $3 to help us keep
building this movement?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260819.gwYTWB&amount=3&refcode=em20260819-6615&t=1003&akid=6615%2E420207%2E0f09Ql ]Contribute $3

Here’s what I know in my bones: we do not suffer from scarcity in this
country. We suffer from greed.

The greed of predatory insurance corporations that rake in billions while
denying care.

The greed of Big Pharma gouging drug prices and leaving working people
with impossible choices, between filling prescriptions and buying
groceries.

The greed of a callous for-profit healthcare system that lets corporate
interests determine who lives and who dies.

And too many working families know exactly what the devastating
consequences of that greed looks like.

85 million Americans are uninsured or underinsured. 1 in 4 can’t afford
their prescription drugs. Over 500,000 families go bankrupt every single
year because of medical debt. And more than 60,000 people die every year
because they cannot afford to see a doctor.

A new Yale study just confirmed what we’ve been saying for years: Medicare
for All would save over 114,000 lives per year and more than $1 trillion
in national health spending.

Where do those savings come from?

* Paying no more than other countries for prescription drugs.
* Cutting the bureaucracy and waste built into a system designed around
insurance company profits, not patient care.
* Curbing fraudulent billing.
* Preventing the emergency room visits that happen when people can't
afford to see a doctor before it's too late.
* Covered preventative care that will keep you out of the ER.

These are the facts that Republicans and their corporate donors don’t want
you to hear, because it threatens their grip on power and their profits.

They can’t win on the facts, so they’re spending billions to keep us
divided, confused, and convinced that change is impossible.

That is a moral catastrophe. And it is completely, utterly preventable.

But change is not impossible,
Peter. Change is inevitable
when we organize for it. We just have to continue fighting and as my
friend Abdul El-Sayed always says, we have to build the political will to
get it done.

And that’s exactly what I’ve done. I’ve been on the ground all summer
knocking on doors, organizing volunteers, and rallying voters alongside
the incredible Medicare For All candidates who won’t back down until
healthcare is guaranteed for every single person in this country.

But I need you with me on this. We win by standing shoulder to shoulder,
and right now, this fight is too big, too important to sit out.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260819.gwYTWB&refcode=em20260819-6615&amount=3&t=1004&akid=6615%2E420207%2E0f09Ql ]If you’re able, will you pitch in $3 or whatever you can
today, to help us make Medicare for All a reality and ensure that no one
in this country ever has to choose between their prescription and food on
their table again?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260819.gwYTWB&amount=3&refcode=em20260819-6615&t=1023&akid=6615%2E420207%2E0f09Ql ]Contribute $3

Thank you for standing with me,

Pramila Jayapal

* * *
Hey folks,
This one is wild. Harry Enten is back at the big board with numbers that spell serious trouble for Donald Trump and Republicans heading into the midterms -- especially with Hispanic men, a group Trump made historic gains with in 2024.
And the collapse isn't just about Trump. It's showing up in how people say they plan to vote.
* [**00:01:03**] Harry breaks down the brutal shift among Hispanic men: from Trump winning them by 10 points in 2024 to a net approval rating of **minus 41**.
* [**00:03:05**] It gets even worse on the economy -- Trump's approval with Hispanic men plunges 49 points underwater, a stunning 60-point swing from 2024.
* [**00:05:13**] Here's the number Republicans should really fear: Hispanic men now favor Democrats for Congress by 20 points, a 28-point swing away from the GOP.
* [**00:07:21**] We zoom out to the national picture, where Trump is underwater in 47 of 50 states -- and talk about what that could mean for Senate and House races across the country.
* [**00:10:10**] After Trump lashes out at CNN reporter Kristen Holmes, I read CNN's response defending her and talk about why attacks on the free press matter.

This episode is about more than one ugly poll. We're watching voters who took a chance on Trump move sharply away from him, while Republicans face the possibility that their own political strategy could backfire spectacularly. But none of these numbers matter unless people actually show up in November. **If you value conversations that cut through the noise and help build something better, help me keep them going.**

Democracy cannot thrive where power remains unchecked and justice is reserved for a select few. Peace cannot exist where justice is not served.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e07b9d8b-b583-4640-8103-e9f66c82e4f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This morning I was in a room with over 2,000 people. Advocates. Educators. Survivors. The National Sexual Assault Conference, right here in Washington DC. And I want to tell you something. I walked in there as an ally and I walked out feeling like I had been plugged into something. You could feel the resilience. You could feel the hope. From every single person there, whether they were a survivor, an advocate, or someone like me who showed up to stand alongside them.
I recently joined the advisory board of Women's HQ. Please check out their website at womenshq.org. They are here for victims and survivors of violence and they offer helping hands to those who need it. I am honored to be part of that work.
I was also there because someone I have come to call a friend was going to be there. And I want to talk about her.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..mt0YRiMCUxiBO5yEoLxUVN4s65blvxPby1gZU-Im9AQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=211924161)
### **GOOD TROUBLEMAKER: ELIZABETH STEIN**
If you know the name Elizabeth Stein, you know why she matters. She is a survivor of Jeffrey Epstein. And she has been loud, and public, and relentless about what she is demanding: accountability. Transparency. Specifically around the Epstein Transparency Act. She has been on the front lines. Standing up for other survivors. Being there for them. Supporting them.
I saw her testify before the Democratic Judiciary Committee in the Senate. That was the first time I got to be in the same room with her. Today I got to see her again. And I have to say, in the months I have been getting to know her, Elizabeth Stein has inspired me.
I am tabbing her as a Good Troublemaker. She is empowering other women. She is being loud when she could be quiet and choosing that path every single day. She is choosing courage when silence would be so much easier.
Elizabeth, keep up the good fight.
### **GOOD TROUBLEMAKER: SUNITA DODDAMANI**
The second person I want to highlight today is a former federal prosecutor. An Assistant US Attorney out of the Eastern District of Michigan. Her name is Sunita Doddamani.
She was fired by the Justice Department. She says it was retaliation, and I believe her. She is suing the Trump administration saying she was unlawfully dismissed for political reasons tied to her work prosecuting cases under the FACE Act. That is the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrants, a federal law that makes it a crime to use force or obstruction to interfere with people seeking or providing reproductive health care.
There have been so many people illegally fired by this administration. FBI agents. Lawyers. DOJ employees. People terminated for nothing other than doing their jobs in ways Donald Trump did not like.
Sunita Doddamani is not taking it lying down.
She is taking a huge risk. When you go after this administration at the legal level, they come back at you. This Justice Department has unlimited resources. And she is not letting that stop her. She is a career prosecutor. She was following the law. She believed in doing her job right. And they fired her for it.
I am giving her special kudos today. Good luck with your lawsuit, Sunita. Keep fighting.
Courage is contagious.
I felt it in that room this morning at the NSAC. I felt it watching Elizabeth Stein walk to the front and speak. I felt it reading about what Sunita Doddamani is doing.
Courage is contagious, y'all. When you see somebody standing up, it makes you want to stand up too. Let's keep getting in good trouble. Necessary trouble.
-Harry

clean_body: The Good Trouble Report | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Good Trouble Report | | | Aug 19 | | | | | | | | | | | | Democracy cannot thrive where power remains unchecked and justice is reserved for a select few. Peace cannot exist where justice is not served. This morning I was in a room with over 2,000 people. Advocates. Educators. Survivors. The National Sexual Assault Conference, right here in Washington DC. And I want to tell you something. I walked in there as an ally and I walked out feeling like I had been plugged into something. You could feel the resilience. You could feel the hope. From every single person there, whether they were a survivor, an advocate, or someone like me who showed up to stand alongside them. I recently joined the advisory board of Women's HQ. Please check out their website at womenshq.org. They are here for victims and survivors of violence and they offer helping hands to those who need it. I am honored to be part of that work. I was also there because someone I have come to call a friend was going to be there. And I want to talk about her. GOOD TROUBLEMAKER: ELIZABETH STEIN If you know the name Elizabeth Stein, you know why she matters. She is a survivor of Jeffrey Epstein. And she has been loud, and public, and relentless about what she is demanding: accountability. Transparency. Specifically around the Epstein Transparency Act. She has been on the front lines. Standing up for other survivors. Being there for them. Supporting them. I saw her testify before the Democratic Judiciary Committee in the Senate. That was the first time I got to be in the same room with her. Today I got to see her again. And I have to say, in the months I have been getting to know her, Elizabeth Stein has inspired me. I am tabbing her as a Good Troublemaker. She is empowering other women. She is being loud when she could be quiet and choosing that path every single day. She is choosing courage when silence would be so much easier. Elizabeth, keep up the good fight. GOOD TROUBLEMAKER: SUNITA DODDAMANI The second person I want to highlight today is a former federal prosecutor. An Assistant US Attorney out of the Eastern District of Michigan. Her name is Sunita Doddamani. She was fired by the Justice Department. She says it was retaliation, and I believe her. She is suing the Trump administration saying she was unlawfully dismissed for political reasons tied to her work prosecuting cases under the FACE Act. That is the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrants, a federal law that makes it a crime to use force or obstruction to interfere with people seeking or providing reproductive health care. There have been so many people illegally fired by this administration. FBI agents. Lawyers. DOJ employees. People terminated for nothing other than doing their jobs in ways Donald Trump did not like. Sunita Doddamani is not taking it lying down. She is taking a huge risk. When you go after this administration at the legal level, they come back at you. This Justice Department has unlimited resources. And she is not letting that stop her. She is a career prosecutor. She was following the law. She believed in doing her job right. And they fired her for it. I am giving her special kudos today. Good luck with your lawsuit, Sunita. Keep fighting. Courage is contagious. I felt it in that room this morning at the NSAC. I felt it watching Elizabeth Stein walk to the front and speak. I felt it reading about what Sunita Doddamani is doing. Courage is contagious, y'all. When you see somebody standing up, it makes you want to stand up too. Let's keep getting in good trouble. Necessary trouble. -Harry P.S. Peter, As we look ahead to the cases the Supreme Court will consider next, one thing is clear: these decisions will be critically important for our democracy, and our rights. **But these cases will be heard by a Supreme Court that has been bought and directed by MAGA special interests.** Trump wants to use SCOTUS as his personal get-out-of-jail card, but the Court is supposed to look out for the people—instead, it’s playing politics and enabling fascists to flout the law. **[Right now, our partners are preparing for the work ahead as we fight to hold this Court accountable to the people, not special interests. Can you fund our fight?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqtuNdrqi4Uvxg7gwLcDD6soan8GzSFVLz__b1P-GgjEIjW2gOwBbG3Or2cfsWOOKc9uYGDMwg8bOKak_mgi_kPhkdJ3N4_ducgFpgLa2_GJWlmJuG1_S8Pbxucg9Nte57VzZXjkeoCsMMap9uHuXFqU2NfrHzQmjgV23qY4ZRWBo4X7EzUqLOMW3kKfRgagnq7RbVNEpaXqOQAVhUxR7dmBu44mx5X8fIU2tPcDlTCfIK13yCkruRDdTm5ys0kbOKlfQ4PzgAYfpaWLFXCLRAZ3DMZzoWO0lR6fkVFD_43HnazYchS7OzpnKz8adcLcvb3xf8MKD2pscoPpVHJYuBeI/4tb/g4zllhqrS96Jtcnz-nd5SQ/h0/h001.LYBKfkdUP1-EmSTmX6iOAPiwBVFx5pxIWik04eJWbvA)** _Let’s look at two of the cases the Court will review this fall to see what’s at stake._ After writer E. Jean Carroll accused Trump of sexual assault, he repeatedly attacked her on social media. She sued for defamation and won an $83.3 million judgement against him. Now Trump’s personal legal team and the federal government have teamed up to ask the Supreme Court to review that judgement, claiming that Trump was entitled to immunity in the Carroll case because his social media attacks were part of his work as president. Another case, _Raycraft v. Lopez-Campos_ , will answer a critical question: _Are non-citizens apprehended within the United States entitled to bond hearings?_ The Trump administration says no, pointing to federal immigration law Section 1225. But that piece of law doesn’t apply to people who are _already_ in the U.S. Another law does, and it clearly allows for the release of detainees on bond. **So, what does Trump want from SCOTUS next?** For his SCOTUS-granted immunity to help him evade accountability for publicly harassing someone he sexually assaulted, and for the Court to allow his administration to detain immigrants without bond, even if the law says otherwise. _In short, to help him flout the law, even if it means denying others their rights._ **This is only possible because our justice system has been captured by a handful of MAGA extremists who are hell-bent on grabbing power over the rest of us, Constitution be damned.** If we don’t work together, every issue we care about will be under attack for decades to come. Only when we all stand together—organizations, experts, activists—can we build the movement that will hold the Supreme Court accountable and win much-needed reform. **That’s why United for Democracy is building the wave to fight back against the dark money interests that have captured the Court.** **[We cannot accept a Supreme Court that could throw our constitutional rights out the window at any moment. name: Rep. Vikki Goodwin
subject: Here's what I heard about healthcare in Sugar Land last night.
disclaimer_text: paid for by the Vikki Goodwin Campaign, Allen Biehl, Treasurer
body:
This is why we're on the road.| | |
---
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137550925/641150162/-742812207?refcode=du_em081926_tc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjNhNTI1YjYtMWU5Yy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8i9PvVV3mlQZAzNjF7Nootairf62UD5o5gWzVXpzeUo=)
---
Peter,
Last night, I stood in a room full of families in Sugar Land and I listened to their experiences with our (lack of) healthcare options in Texas.
I heard story after story of people doing everything right — working hard, paying their bills — and still falling through the cracks of a healthcare system that was never built for them.
That was our first stop on the [**Texas Cares Tour**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137550926/641150163/-742812207?refcode=du_em081926_tc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjNhNTI1YjYtMWU5Yy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8i9PvVV3mlQZAzNjF7Nootairf62UD5o5gWzVXpzeUo=), and it made one thing absolutely clear:
**Healthcare is simply not accessible for these families.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137550927/641150164/-742812207?refcode=du_em081926_tc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjNhNTI1YjYtMWU5Yy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8i9PvVV3mlQZAzNjF7Nootairf62UD5o5gWzVXpzeUo=)
---
When I told them about Texas Cares — real Medicaid expansion, options for families who earn too much for Medicaid and too little for private insurance, and a state-run option that covers vision, dental, mental health, and pre-existing conditions —******the room lit up.**
People had questions. _Good ones._ They wanted to know the details, and they were excited because for the first time, someone was offering them a real plan instead of excuses.
[**That's what's on the line in this race.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137550928/641150165/-742812207?refcode=du_em081926_tc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjNhNTI1YjYtMWU5Yy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8i9PvVV3mlQZAzNjF7Nootairf62UD5o5gWzVXpzeUo=)
Dan Patrick has blocked Medicaid expansion for twelve years. That's costing Texas $10 billion a year — money we send to Washington and hand to other states _while 5.1 million Texans go without coverage._
**We can't afford another year of his leadership.**
---
[ **🚐 FUEL THE TOUR** ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137550929/641150166/-742812207?refcode=du_em081926_tc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjNhNTI1YjYtMWU5Yy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8i9PvVV3mlQZAzNjF7Nootairf62UD5o5gWzVXpzeUo=)
---
The Sugar Land townhall was just the beginning. We're heading to Beaumont today, and then through East Texas — because every community in Texas deserves to know they have a champion fighting for them.
[But keeping this tour on the road takes resources. If last night's stories moved you like they moved me, please chip in right now. **Every dollar helps us reach one more community. One more family. clean_body: This is why we're on the road.| | | | | | = Peter, Last night, I stood in a room full of families in Sugar Land and I listened to their experiences with our (lack of) healthcare options in Texas. I heard story after story of people doing everything right — working hard, paying their bills — and still falling through the cracks of a healthcare system that was never built for them. That was our first stop on the =, and it made one thing absolutely clear: Healthcare is simply not accessible for these families. = When I told them about Texas Cares — real Medicaid expansion, options for families who earn too much for Medicaid and too little for private insurance, and a state-run option that covers vision, dental, mental health, and pre-existing conditions —****the room lit up. People had questions. Good ones. They wanted to know the details, and they were excited because for the first time, someone was offering them a real plan instead of excuses. = Dan Patrick has blocked Medicaid expansion for twelve years. That's costing Texas $10 billion a year — money we send to Washington and hand to other states while 5.1 million Texans go without coverage. We can't afford another year of his leadership. = The Sugar Land townhall was just the beginning. There has to be a better way."
The "better way," according to Democrats, is to have almost no enforcement of immigration law. Friend,

The Democrat Party is being taken over by self-described socialists, and it's happening right now, primary after primary.

name: Mary Peltola
subject: I’m officially running in the general election for U.S. Senate in Alaska
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260819-1.uCSfpr&refcode=em20260819-3716&t=1&akid=3716%2E21716%2EDUiuFg)
Hello,
My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday’s primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.
I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Congresswoman Sarah McBride:
**[Contribute »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260819-1.uCSfpr&refcode=em20260819-3716&t=2&akid=3716%2E21716%2EDUiuFg)**
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
[**Please split a contribution between Congresswoman Sarah McBride and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260819-1.uCSfpr&refcode=em20260819-3716&t=3&akid=3716%2E21716%2EDUiuFg)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260819-1.uCSfpr&amount=5&refcode=em20260819-3716&t=22&akid=3716%2E21716%2EDUiuFg)**
Thank you,
Mary

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: We just learned that we are polling only one point behind Greg Abbott. This is the tightest margin of Abbott’s entire political life.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
Taking back Texas this year is in our sights.
Friend —
I need you to sit with this number for a second: **one point.**
That's it. That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News.
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260819_2_ak.slnyCr&amount=5&refcode=em20260819-721&t=2&akid=721%2E127862%2EOqw-xh)
In nearly twelve years as governor, through three elections, Greg Abbott has never faced a poll this close. _Not once._ His campaign has already spent over $54 million this cycle just to hang on to power. This poll says people aren’t buying what he’s selling anymore.
Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Nearly 4 in 10 Texans say inflation is the top issue on their minds — **and after 12 years of Greg Abbott, they're done waiting around for things to get better.**
I'm not surprised. I've been hearing it at every stop — from Brownsville to Austin to Amarillo. Families are tired of watching their grocery bills and insurance premiums climb while Abbott hands billions to his donors.
**This 1-point poll shows that a new chapter for Texas is finally in reach.** But it’s not guaranteed. Turnout will decide this election. And Abbott's team knows it — they're going to spend the next 76 days doing everything they can to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up to the polls to vote. They will do anything to keep Texans from turning the page on his failed administration.
I can't outspend Greg Abbott, and I don’t need to. Our campaign can out-organize him, but that takes people like you stepping up right now to raise the resources we need to win this race.
**[Can you chip in $5 split between Aaron Ford and my campaign to help us keep closing this gap and — finally — take back Texas?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260819_2_ak.slnyCr&amount=5&refcode=em20260819-721&t=3&akid=721%2E127862%2EOqw-xh)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260819_2_ak.slnyCr&amount=5&refcode=em20260819-721&t=22&akid=721%2E127862%2EOqw-xh)**
We've never been this close. Let's make sure we don't waste this opportunity.
Gina
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260819_2_ak.slnyCr&amount=5&refcode=em20260819-721&t=23&akid=721%2E127862%2EOqw-xh)

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_af_footer?refcode=em20260819-721-&t=24&refcode2=721_127862_Oqw-xh&akid=721%2E127862%2EOqw-xh)**
